## Agent tools and harness

The read, edit and bash tools, the driver, the loop and its checks.

#### The edit tool needs the exact hard-wrapped text of ~79-column files
Where: the edit tool on tasks/*.md, PLAN.md (any markdown that is hard-wrapped at ~79 characters)
Symptom: an edit call is rejected (oldText "not found") although the text looks identical when read -
the file hard-wraps prose, so one sentence spans several physical lines, and a rendered or `head`
view shows different breaks than the file actually holds (the task-000 edits to 212 were rejected
this way at iteration 12; landed at iteration 13).
Why/fix: capture the exact bytes first: `sed -n 'A,Bp' <file> | cat -A`, and copy the physical lines
verbatim (wrap points and indentation included) into oldText.

#### edit tool "Could not find" on a byte-verified oldText: the call's parameters were mangled, not the file
Where: the edit tool (any file)
Symptom: an edit call is rejected with "Could not find ..." although `od -An -tx1` on the target line
shows oldText matches the file byte-for-byte; a batch call dies on one entry (the rest are NOT applied,
the file is untouched - `git diff` empty), and the same text matches later when the call arrives well
formed.
Why/fix: this is an accident in how the tool call was encoded (one call in the same session had the whole
`edits` argument arrive as a JSON string instead of an array, rejected by validation; the failing batch
entries were in the same shape), not a file-content mismatch. Do not conclude from a "not found" that the
file differs from your notes - od the line, then retry the same text in smaller entries with short unique
anchors (iteration 174, 236a: the 9-edit batch for tests/test_src_us_cities.py "failed atomically" twice;
every line matched once the parameters arrived clean).

#### A task file's own section name appears mid-line in its Notes - naive str.index splits there and destroys the file
Where: any python rewrite of a tasks/*.md `## Hand-over` tail section, when the file's Notes/Goal cites the section name mid-sentence (307ba's Notes: "...in the parent 307b's ## Hand-over and the 2026-10-12 307b DECISIONS entry...")
Symptom: `t.index("## Hand-over")` hits the mid-line reference in Notes, so `t[:i] + new_section` splices the new hand-over into the middle of the Notes bullet: the rest of that sentence and every following Notes bullet are silently lost, and the new section ends up header-less (iteration 120, 307ba: three of four Notes bullets lost)
Why/fix: split on the line-anchored marker instead: `re.search(r"^## Hand-over\n", t, re.M)` (or grep -n '^## Hand-over'). After replacing a file's tail section, verify with `git diff --stat` plus a read of the sections ABOVE the edit point (the Notes bullets, the acceptance boxes) to catch a mid-line splice.

#### The read tool's output of fit/src_van_deventer.py is not byte-faithful - source edit oldText from sed/grep
Where: the read tool on `fit/src_van_deventer.py` (and any edit call whose oldText came from its view)
Symptom: an edit call is rejected (oldText "not found") although the read-tool view looks identical - the
view dropped a word (204 iter 52: it showed "21 to stage + 2 done" where the file has "21 to stage + the 2
done"; two edit calls failed on it)
Why/fix: the read tool's rendering of that long file is not byte-for-byte reliable. Capture the exact physical
lines with `sed -n 'N,Mp'` / `grep -n` and copy them verbatim into oldText (iter 53's 28 sed-derived blocks
and iter 54's 7 lead-doc blocks all applied clean on the first try).

#### A new top-level task number can be claimed in two checkouts at once
Where: creating tasks/<N>-<name>.md in team mode (each agent in its own branch; the driver merges main in before each session)
Symptom: two files with the same number sit in tasks/ after a sync (iteration 109: the lead's 309-queue-right-place.md and agent a's 309-place-check.md, created 5 minutes apart, neither session seeing the other's commit)
Why/fix: a number is only free inside your own checkout; a concurrent lead/agent commit on main can claim the same number before your session's merge. After the driver's main-sync, before creating a new task file, `ls tasks/` and check the driver's prompt (it names the in-flight tasks by number and title); on a collision, the file created first - or the one the prompt names - is canonical: set yours to Status: dropped and keep its content as reference.

#### A session can start in the main worktree; the agent's own checkout is a sibling worktree
Where: the team-mode checkouts /home/agent/projects/ancient-works (main), ancient-works.a (agent/a), ancient-works.c (agent/c) - linked worktrees of ONE repo (git-common-dir = ancient-works/.git)
Symptom: `git status` in the cwd says "On branch main" although the prompt says you are agent c, and files you committed on your branch (e.g. tools/right_place.py) are absent from the cwd's working tree
Why/fix: the worktrees share refs but have different checkouts; an agent's branch commits are checked out only in that agent's worktree. At session start run `git branch` and `git worktree list` in the cwd; if the cwd is the main worktree (or another agent's), do all work in and commit in your own worktree directory (agent c: /home/agent/projects/ancient-works.c). Never commit work in the main worktree.
#### A Depends-on line pointing at a SPLIT parent parks (a subtask pointing at its own parent deadlocks)
Where: the driver's task queue in team mode; any `Depends on:` naming a task whose Status is `split`
Symptom: the dependent task sits in Tasks-in-flight (open) and is never handed out (agent c's 804/805 at iterations 97-98: both depended on their own split parent 309; both parked until the dep lines were rewritten)
Why/fix: a split parent becomes done only AFTER its subtasks finish, so a subtask depending on its parent is a cycle; an outsider depending on it waits for the whole chain to close. Point the dep at the LAST subtask in the chain (805, not 309) - unless the parent is the only driver-visible name (agent a's 220, iteration 117: kept `Depends on: 309` because 804/805 existed only on agent/c's branch and the driver's prompt names the parent; 309's post-805 closure adds no store change, so the extra wait is bookkeeping-only).

#### .agent/reports/last-test-output.txt can be a day STALE - stat it before chasing its failures
Where: `.agent/reports/last-test-output.txt`, `.agent/reports/last-failing-tests.txt`, the dated driver notes in PROGRESS.md
Symptom: the "current" suite report lists failures that no longer exist (2026-10-12, 309/805: the report, mtime 2026-10-11 17:14, listed three shotwick orphans; the current tree - shotwick since built into sites.json, the named untracked item gone - passes all of them)
Why: the driver writes these files when it runs the suite at a loop start, but that run is not every iteration; a file can be a day old while the tree behind it merges on and moves (a day of merges here rebuilt sites.json and the review data).
What to do: `stat -c '%n %y' .agent/reports/*.txt` and cross-check the dates of the driver notes in PROGRESS; then run the suite yourself (`.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/`) before believing or fixing anything the report says.

#### A /tmp asset derived from a per-site file must be suffixed with the doc's plan id - two docs of one site share a site-prefixed name
Where: audit-script judging crops (tools/audit_306c.mjs's helpers, e.g. /tmp/crop_<site>_{a,r}.png); any throwaway script deriving /tmp assets from per-site files when a site carries several docs
Symptom: judging the 2nd doc of a site silently reads the 1st doc's crop - 306c misattributed the 8-marker hodgen-s-cemetery-mound crop to n0092 when it was n0353's; the near-identical anchors survived a visual check
Why: the site is the natural naming key, but a site has multiple docs (hodgen-s-cemetery-mound has 2 in 306c); the second write overwrites the first. Key /tmp assets by the full doc id (site + plan) and regenerate on demand from the committed docs/site_flow/agent_fits/ shots - the map pane is a crop (1040, 0, w, 880) of the 1440x900 shot at 2.6x LANCZOS, so the repo shots are always the re-derivable source of truth.

#### web_fetch returns page TEXT without image URLs - curl the raw HTML and grep src/data-src for picture URLs
Where: the web_fetch tool; any HTML page whose pictures come from HTML attributes (Wikimedia Commons File: pages with lazy-loaded thumbnails)
Symptom: asking web_fetch for "the file URL" / "the image" of a page returns the readable text (description, metadata, captions) with no image URLs at all, so the needed upload.wikimedia.org / archive.org path is unobtainable through the tool
Why/how: the tool returns a text extraction, and images are only referenced in markup (`src`, or `data-src` on lazy-loaded thumbnails). Curl the page instead and grep the attributes: `curl -s <url> | grep -o 'src="[^"]*"\|data-src="[^"]*"' | head` - a Commons file page carries the canonical image URL in the preview `src` and the "Original file" link (306d/306e used this for Commons file pages while judging orphan docs).

#### A lead block on main can LAG an agent branch: a session in the gap works on a "blocked" task in good faith
Where: team-mode task files; the main merge that conflicts in the task's own Status line (207a iters 202/203: the lead blocked 207a/207b on main at 11:19 after the owner's "Stop 207"; agent/c's last main merge was 09:36, so iteration 202 ran fetch work on the branch before the block was visible there)
Symptom: the driver's pre-session merge of main conflicts in exactly your task file: main's side = `Status: blocked` + a "## Lead note" ("the owner said ... . Do not start until the owner lifts it."), your side = `Status: in-progress` + your hand-over; loop.log: "team: main conflicts with <branch> in: tasks/<t>.md - the next session resolves it"
Why/how: the lead posts the owner's decisions to main; an agent's branch only sees them at the driver's pre-session merge. A session that starts in the gap between that merge and the lead's commit works on the task without knowing it is stopped - work completed in the window (e.g. a finished fetch) is usually harmless, but the next expensive step must not be started. Resolution when the merge lands: keep both sides' intent - main's `Status: blocked` + the lead note VERBATIM, then your hand-over (what is done + a verbatim resume recipe) after it; file a BLOCKING ask_human confirming the stop still stands (a blocked task waits only while its request is open - an open request is what stops the driver's blocked-without-request flip that re-hand-outs the task, as it did here 30 min after the lead's block). The parked work resumes only when the owner lifts the stop (answer or a lead unblock on main).

#### A hand-over can claim files "created" that never reached disk when the session was cut - verify previous sessions' claims against the working tree before building on them
Where: any `## Hand-over` in tasks/*.md (302, iteration 207: the hand-over claimed subtasks 302e/302f/302g were "created", but the driver's post-207 commit touched only the parent file - the subtask writes never landed, and iteration 208 had to write them for real)
Symptom: the hand-over says "created subtasks X/Y/Z" / "wrote file F", but `ls tasks/` shows no such file and the last session's commits touch only the task file itself
Why/how: a session can be cut after (or without) the file writes it described, and the hand-over is the next agent's first truth. Verify every "done/created" claim against the working tree before acting on it (`ls tasks/`, `git log --oneline -- <path>`, re-run the claimed command), and when writing several new files in one session, write the durable artifacts first and the hand-over last - a hand-over that outlives its own claims poisons the next session.

#### In team mode each checkout has its OWN /tmp/loop-<checkout> TMPDIR (separate pytest basetemps) - but /tmp trees are short-lived under two independent wipers; never plan around /tmp retention
Where: the harness (per-checkout TMPDIR=/tmp/loop-<checkout-dir>; verified 2026-10-13: agent a -> /tmp/loop-ancient-works.a, agent c -> /tmp/loop-ancient-works.c, and no bare /tmp/loop-<project> dir); pytest 9.1.1 (basetemp $TMPDIR/pytest-of-<user>, tmp_path_retention_policy=failed, count=1); the loop's disk-pressure maintenance (the /tmp/loop-* wipe entry under This machine and its environment); tests/test_owner_check.py's private trees (ownerA0/ownerB0/awowner0)
Symptom: evidence trees in a checkout's /tmp/loop-<checkout>/pytest-of-agent are gone when checked - 2026-10-13 (307d): the ninth session's retained tree was gone before the tenth session, and the tenth session's own run trees were gone by the time the eleventh session looked (by 14:58 both checkouts' loop dirs held only jiti/node-compile-cache). The tenth session's hand-over blamed "agent c's concurrent runs" and claimed /tmp/pytest-of-agent is SHARED by every agent's pytest sessions - not supported: the per-checkout TMPDIRs make the basetemps separate, so another agent's pytest cannot touch this checkout's.
Why: wipers make /tmp trees short-lived without any other agent involved: (1) a GREEN pytest session rmtree's its whole checkout basetemp at session end and prunes older numbered dirs (retention policy=failed, count=1; see the "Two pytest sessions of one checkout trash each other's temp trees" entry) - so a run that just finished green leaves nothing behind, and a second run started in the same checkout can destroy a still-running one (the tenth session ran its tests green and then a background full suite - that alone explains its own evidence vanishing); (2) the loop's maintenance wipes /tmp/loop-*/pytest-of-agent ACROSS all checkouts when the disk nears full - the wildcard ignores the checkout isolation; (3) a SESSION-BOUNDARY wipe (the 2026-10-15 812 case): a nohup full-suite run started 08:10 in the previous session lost its basetemp at ~08:22, the moment the NEXT session started (driver commits at 08:21:34-47; /tmp/loop-ancient-works.a recreated by 08:22-08:23) with the disk at 70% - so the harness clears the checkout's /tmp/loop-<checkout> namespace at session start, out from under any still-running background process of the previous session. New symptom vs (1)/(2): a test's first `tmp_path_factory.mktemp` dies with `FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] .../pytest-0` (pytest 9.1.1's make_numbered_dir scans the basetemp root before creating it - os.scandir ENOENT), erroring the whole module at setup even though every test before the wipe passed; servers left with deleted docroots give HTTPError 404, and subprocess trees give bare FileNotFoundError. Which wiper fired at a given moment cannot be identified afterwards (no process, no log).
What to do: dump evidence into the repo (the 307d pattern: screenshots into docs/site_flow/, the server runlog into the run's outdir) or read it in the session that made it; never carry a plan that assumes a /tmp tree survives a session boundary, a following green run, or a disk-pressure event. For a run that MUST outlive its session, start it outside the wiped namespace: `nohup env TMPDIR=/tmp/aw-<stable-dir-you-manage> .venv/bin/python -m pytest ... > /tmp/<log>` (tests carry no hard-coded /tmp paths - verified 2026-10-15, they follow TMPDIR via tmp_path_factory; bare /tmp already proved it survives wipes: the it.246 log did). The it.247 run did exactly this (TMPDIR=/tmp/aw-it247-tmp, log /tmp/iter247-full.log).

#### The driver's scheduler tokenizes EVERY `NNN`/`NNNx` on the `Depends on:` line, prose included - a self-mention parks the task forever
Where: the one-line `Depends on:` in tasks/*.md (tasks/README.md: the driver reads that line as the task's dependencies); team-mode scheduling and the done-claim re-check
Symptom: the driver reopens a done claim with "Team project: these tasks can never start, their `Depends on:` lines wait on each other: 212 (waits on 212 235), 239 (waits on 212 238 302f 302g)" - the "212" in the prose "212's done re-claim" inside a parenthetical made 212 depend on ITSELF, and 239 (a legitimate wait on 212) parked behind it; the driver's "waits on" list is exactly the PENDING subset of the parsed tokens (done ids like 203a/301/306e are parsed but dropped from the note)
Why: the line is machine-parsed for task-id tokens, not read as prose - any number in an explanation counts as a dependency, and the format spec (a bare comma list or `none`) exists so the parser never sees prose. A `NNNx` self-token is a self-loop (can never start); a `(none - a record; ... 307b/307c ...)` tokenizes as real deps on the wrong direction.
What to do: keep the line a bare comma-separated id list (or `none`); put the why in the hand-over or DECISIONS.md (000 iteration 158 stripped the prose from 212, 212a, 307a - the rationales already lived in each file's hand-over, so only the lines changed; verify with a token scan that no pending task is in a cycle before claiming a plan done).

#### Editing a file the test suite hashes mid-run fails its integrity checks (the working tree must be stable while pytest runs)
Where: any in-flight full-suite run (`.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/ ...`) in this checkout vs. edits to files inside its snapshot set: data/ (minus the raw symlink), web/data top level, docs/, specs/, tests/ (tests/test_cover.py::test_checkout_integrity snapshots before/after the cover run; other tests assert on committed content of the same dirs)
Symptom: `FAILED tests/test_cover.py::test_checkout_integrity - AssertionError: checkout files changed by the phases: ['docs/lead_roman.md']` with before/after sha256 differing - even though nothing in the run itself touched the file; 2026-10-14 (808) hit it by appending the lead accounting to docs/lead_roman.md while the suite was running in the same checkout.
Why/fix: the suite takes file snapshots at test start and compares at test end; a human/agent edit in between reads as "the run changed it". Commit (or defer) every working-tree edit BEFORE starting a verification run, and never start a long run while you still plan to edit: re-run the suite on the stable tree - the red that looks like your data change is usually just your own keystrokes. (Team mode note: other checkouts run their own suites, but TMPDIR is per-checkout, so cross-checkout interference is not the cause - this one is self-inflicted.)

#### A saved PIL crop of a Wikimedia thumb can render blank in the read tool while a resize of the same file renders fine
Where: the read tool + PIL crop/resize saves of ~1280 px Commons thumbs (the research thumb-eyeballing workflow)
Symptom: `Image.open(thumb).crop(box).save(x.jpg)` produces a file the read tool renders as a uniformly dark/blank image, although a pixel probe (`px[x, y]`) of the same region shows bright, correct values; re-running the identical crop fails the same way, while `im.resize(same_size).crop(same_box)` and a read of the untouched source both render correctly (2026-10-14, 240 Minneapolis research: two direct crops of the 1885 Minneapolis thumb rendered blank, resize-then-crop and the full-image resize rendered fine; no EXIF data involved).
Why/fix: cause not established (the JPEG writer, the read tool's decode, or their interaction). When a saved crop renders blank, probe the source pixels to confirm the content is there, then re-derive the view from `im.resize(...)` before cropping (or just re-read the original file) instead of debugging the encoder; the resize-then-crop workaround is byte-stable enough for eyeballing.

#### `pkill -f` inside a bash tool call kills the call's own shell when the pattern appears anywhere in the script (it matches `bash -c <entire script>`) - looks exactly like an external preemption, but is self-inflicted
Where: any harness bash tool call containing a `pkill -f <pattern>` whose pattern string also occurs in the script's own text (e.g. the quoted path of a background helper named in a later nohup line); the harness records the result as "(no output)" + "Command exited with code 143" with no cause
Symptom: the call dies a few seconds after start; nothing after the pkill line ever runs (no files created, no processes, not even the next command's redirection target); no external killer is findable (the driver's .agent/loop.log is silent after session start, no OOM in dmesg, a bare `sleep 65` with the same timeout survives) - so it reads as the loop's "kills competing in-flight runs" preemption (the entry above), but it is self-inflicted. Hit 2026-10-15 (247, iteration 218): `pkill -f "aw-247-218/watch.py"` while starting an evidence watcher before a full-suite run; the run never started, and the false preemption hypothesis cost the investigation.
Why: `pkill -f` matches against the FULL command line of every process; the tool's shell is `bash -c <entire script text>`, and the pattern occurs in that text (in the pkill line's own quotes and in the later line that names the helper), so pkill signals its own parent shell with SIGTERM (its default) right after signalling the intended target; the shell dies before the following lines run, and the harness only records the 143.
What to do: kill background helpers by pid - record `$!` to a pid file at start (`nohup ... & echo $! > /tmp/<lane>/<name>.pid`) and later `kill $(cat /tmp/<lane>/<name>.pid)`; if name matching is unavoidable, use a pattern the current script does not literally contain and check `ps -eo pid,args` for the intended victim first.

#### On this VM the LiDAR relief tiles are off for good: server/relief_tiles.py imports the Mac-only `aw` module
Where: `server/relief_tiles.py`, `server/serve.py` (`--port 0` runs, headless page loads)
Symptom: `relief tiles off (aw not importable); run with .venv/bin/python for the LiDAR relief layer` once in
serve.py's stdout; the page's `/tiles/relief/*` requests 404 in every headless run on this machine
`aw` (the owner's private relief renderer, `aw.render_relief`) exists only on the owner's Mac. serve.py prints the
line once and serves without the route; the page tolerates it (the aerial imagery still loads) and the headless
tests treat `/tiles/` reqfails as the only allowed failures. Don't try to "fix" it: relief tile generation is
impossible here, only the owner's machine renders relief.

#### The page's base imagery is a live Esri feed: no-internet headless runs always get ERR_ABORTED on it, and its URL segment is the SINGULAR 'tile/'
Where: `web/index.html` (base imagery source ~line 314: `https://server.arcgisonline.com/ArcGIS/rest/services/World_Imagery/MapServer/tile/{z}/{y}/{x}`), every headless page test that asserts on reqfail lines (tests/test_fit_queue.py card tests, tests/test_review.py, 307bb's part 4)
Symptom: `[reqfail] https://server.arcgisonline.com/.../MapServer/tile/... net::ERR_ABORTED` lines in headless runs (they land while a fetch is in flight at a map-view change or teardown, so an unexcluded test fails on some runs and not others)
The page requests this live feed, so in a no-network run these fetches die, and on this VM (which HAS internet - a tile answers 200 in 0.2 s, verified 2026-10-12 in task 306b) the probes' rapid map teardown aborts in-flight tiles instead (see the web/ entry on the same feed): either way a page-caused abort, the same allowed class as the relief-tile aborts above, to be excluded in reqfail assertions. Excluding by path alone is NOT enough: the Esri path segment is the singular 'tile/' (`MapServer/tile/`), which the common `'/tiles/' not in url` filter misses - exclude by host instead: `'/tiles/' not in ln and 'arcgisonline' not in ln`.

#### The driver's .venv build needs a fully pinned and hashed requirements.txt
Where: `requirements.in`, `requirements.txt`, the driver's venv build (`pip install --require-hashes`)
Symptom: `ERROR: In --require-hashes mode, all requirements must have their versions pinned with ==. These do not: ...`
Fix: add the package to `requirements.in`, regenerate `requirements.txt` with `pip-compile --generate-hashes`
from a throwaway venv outside the project (pip-tools itself goes there, e.g. `/tmp/aw-pto`), commit both.
PyPI is reachable from this machine and cp312 wheels for the current requirements install fine (2026-10-10:
the built `.venv` ran the 8-test suite). 2026-10-11 (302a): scikit-image==0.26.0 was pinned (deps imageio==2.38.1,
lazy-loader==0.6, networkx==3.7) for fit/inkfit.py; pip-compile re-resolved all other pins unchanged, and
the rebuilt .venv ran the full suite (59 passed, 1 pre-existing failure, see the gate_heldout entry below).

#### A driver PROGRESS note about a shared file may describe main, not your checkout
Where: `PROGRESS.md` (project-wide driver notes), any shared file (e.g. `requirements.txt`)
Symptom: a driver note reports a build/test failure (e.g. `ERROR: In --require-hashes mode,
all requirements must have their versions pinned with ==. These do not:`) but your checkout's
copy of the file is fine and your local runs work.
Why: the driver rebuilds from main, while your branch may carry a newer copy of the file that
has not been merged (requirements.txt: the pinned compiled version was committed on agent/c at
iteration 1; main still has the unpinned source list from e2d4060). Checking only the working
tree (as iteration 6 did) says "stale"; `git diff origin/main -- <file>` and
`git show origin/main:<file>` is the real check. If the file is not in your task's Touches,
file a task for its owner (done: tasks/800-requirements-pinned.md) instead of "fixing" it.
Merges only land a branch's copy of a shared file when it differs from the merge base:
compare `git rev-parse <base|main|branch>:<file>` at all three tips (800: base == main ==
93511f2, branch fda2210 -> the merge lands the pinned file cleanly; had the branch blob
matched the base, the merge would silently keep main's copy).

#### The driver's done-claim baseline is its own newest loop-start suite note, not your checkout's state at your task's start
Where: the driver's done-claim re-check (AGENTS.md "Done"), the "test suite failing at loop start (N tests)" notes in `PROGRESS.md`, tests that key on the shared store (`tests/test_batch_eu.py` union checks, `tests/test_serve.py::test_platefits_docs_match_sites`)
Symptom: a done claim is rejected with "Tests failing that were not failing before this task: <list>" although your checkout has carried exactly those reds for many iterations and you compared against an OLDER loop-start note that also listed them (302a session 7, 2026-10-12: the three shotwick-orphan reds - the older 4-red note listed them, the driver's newest 1-red note did not).
Why: the driver re-verifies against its own most recent loop-start suite run (the newest such note in PROGRESS.md), and that run is taken on a tree that may predate the shared store's current state (e.g. before a doc landed in data/db/platefits) - no live checkout necessarily mirrors it. A red caused by shared-store state (an orphan doc pointing at a site unbuilt in web/data/sites.json, etc.) therefore counts as a NEW failure for every claim until the task that owns the file (211 for web/data/sites.json) merges.
What to do: before claiming done, diff your failing tests against the NEWEST "loop start" note only - not against an older one, not against your recollection. If a red is owned by another open task's file, add that task to your `Depends on:` line, commit, and end the session (no stand-ins); the driver brings the task back when the dependency merges, when the suite should be re-run and the claim re-made.

#### sudo on this machine is passwordless for apt-get only
Where: any `sudo` command (sudoers.d/agent-apt; AGENTS.md's "system packages install with `sudo apt-get install -y`")
Symptom: `sudo -n true` (or any non-apt command) → `sudo: a password is required`; plain `sudo` without a TTY hangs/asks for a password.
Why and what to do: the agent user's sudoers rule whitelists apt-get only. System installs must go through apt: download the package to /tmp, then `sudo -n apt-get install -y /tmp/<pkg>.deb` (apt resolves and installs the dependencies). Tools that shell out to a generic `sudo` fail here — e.g. `npx playwright@1.63.0 install chrome` (its reinstall script runs `apt-get` via a sudo that wants a TTY).

#### shot.mjs's `[console]` 404 lines carry no URL, one per failed request - a probe that re-fetches an expected-404 path inflates any count assertion
Where: `tools/shot.mjs` (logs every console message as `[console] <type> <text>`), `tests/test_review.py` (the n404 count assertion)
Symptom: a headless test asserting "exactly two `[console] error ... 404` lines per page load" fails with four - the probe's own in-page check loop re-fetched the two expected-404 paths (data/scans.json, data/amazon/areas.json), and Chrome logs one line per failed request, not per unique URL.
Why: the browser's network line ("Failed to load resource: ... 404 (File not found)") prints no URL at all, so a count cannot be attributed to a path. In this tree the page's boot fetches exactly those two paths, once each (verified 2026-10-11 with a throwaway node script carrying a `page.on('response')` URL logger: a bare load produced exactly those two 404s, stable across runs; adding the probe's re-fetches made four).
What to do: in probes that assert the 404 count, re-fetch only paths that must return 200; check expected-404 paths through the count itself, or attribute them with a throwaway node script that logs `page.on('response')` (URLs come free).

#### shot.mjs's `[js]` probe is evaluated as an EXPRESSION: a bare `async () => {...}` string returns undefined and never runs
Where: `tools/shot.mjs` (`page.evaluate(js)`), every `[js]` probe argument (e.g. 306a's tools/audit_306a.mjs audit driver)
Symptom: the `[eval]` line prints `undefined` and the page did nothing - no `[pageerror]`, no visible effect. Throwing the bare string at a throwaway probe page shows it: `page.evaluate('async () => ({a:42})')` -> undefined, while `page.evaluate('(async () => ({a:42})())')` -> `{"a":42}`.
Why/fix: Playwright 1.63 treats a string argument to `page.evaluate` as a JavaScript EXPRESSION to evaluate, not a function body; a bare function literal evaluates to a function value (serialized to undefined) and is never invoked. Always wrap probe code in an IIFE: `js = '(async () => { ... })()'`.

#### Long background data jobs outlive sessions - check the writer before committing or trusting its file
Where: nohup'd background runs (e.g. 213's /tmp/civitates_triage.py over data/books/triage/*.jsonl), append-only jsonl data files, the driver's "uncommitted work after iteration N" snapshot commits

#### `open(path, "w")` truncates the file BEFORE the argument expression is evaluated - a failing arg can destroy it
Where: any inline `python3 - <<EOF` (or one-liner) that writes a file, e.g. rewriting a section of a markdown/text file
Symptom: `open(path, "w").writelines(lines[:n] + open(other))` - the target is truncated to EMPTY the instant
      `open(path, "w")` is evaluated, and if the argument expression then raises (here: `list + file` is a TypeError),
      the file is left empty; the session's only working copy of it is gone (only git has the committed version).
Why: Python evaluates the receiver expression (`open(path,"w")` - whose side effect is the truncation) before the
      argument expression, so a TypeError raised while building the argument has already emptied the file. Compute the
      whole new content into a variable FIRST (and `assert`/validate it), and only call the write as the final step.
      When a file is precious and uncommitted, keep a backup copy or stage to a temp path and `mv` it in.

#### NFKD on this machine does NOT apply Unicode compatibility (F-type) decompositions
Where: `unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", ...)` anywhere on this machine - `pipeline/catalog.py`'s `slug()`,
      `pipeline/books_match.py`'s `norm()`, and hence every site id built from a town name (`fit/
      src_van_deventer.py`'s `_site_row`)
Symptom: the compatibility chars U+0153 œ, U+0152 Œ, U+00E6 æ, U+00C6 Æ, U+00DF ß survive NFKD and are then
      dropped by `.encode("ascii", "ignore")` - "Le Rœulx" slugs to "le-rulx" (not "le-roeulx"), so the
      staged site id is `le-rulx-q668861`.
Why: CPython 3.12.3 here (Unicode 15.0.0) applies only canonical (D-type) decompositions: é/è/à decompose,
      œ/æ/ß do not (verified against explicit code points). The behaviour is consistent across the whole
      pipeline on this machine, so ids built from `catalog.slug` are internally consistent - do not
      "fix" one name with a per-name override: that would break the one-place rule for the slug rule and
      desync from every other slugification of the same name.

#### The gitignored data (data/raw and the per-site web/data/sites dirs) is a SHARED store: every checkout symlinks it into the main checkout, so parallel agents rewrite each other's files
Where: `data/raw` (one symlink to /home/agent/projects/ancient-works/data/raw), `web/data/sites/<site>/` (382 per-site symlinks there, the 6 tracked hand-fitted site dirs, plus the untracked real dir shotwick-castle-q7502621 - built in a checkout that has no shared-store copy of it, so it never got a symlink), tests/test_site_done.py, /home/agent/projects/ancient-works (the main-branch checkout)
Symptom: a byte-compare test against a per-site file fails with content your checkout never wrote (2026-10-11, test_site_done: `At index 35 diff: b'p' != b'm'` - the rebuilt depictions.json has the 7 plan entries, the comparison target only the 2 maps), while `git status` is clean; `git check-ignore` answers "pathspec ... is beyond a symbolic link"; the target file's mtime (stat -c %y) points at a moment inside another agent's session, not yours.
Why: each agent checkout symlinks its gitignored data into the main checkout's copy - the machine's one image/scan store (data/raw's GB of book scans and the rebuilt per-site directories). Any agent's (or the lead/driver's) run rewrites those shared files in place, and concurrent checkouts see each other's churn: 301 (agent c) was mid-flight re-running Stonehenge through the new site line, resetting the shared depictions.json to the pre-sync state, which voided test_site_done's byte compare transiently.
What to do: diagnose with `readlink web/data/sites/<site>` (target = the main checkout), `stat -c %y` on the target (who wrote it when), and `git status`/`git branch` in the other checkout (who was mid-work). If the failing file is outside your Touches, record it as transient shared-store churn (DECISIONS + hand-over) and re-check when the other task lands - never "fix" the other task's test or the shared store from your task.
