Do not burn attempts re-trying the tunnel; code that needs Clef (picture classification) must take an injectable classifier and, in a working phase, ask the human (a tunnel from a machine that has shell access, or an approved one-off substitute) instead of failing. The 211 pictures do not need it (they are already in data/commons/classified.jsonl) - only brand-new files would.
### Internet Archive (archive.org)

#### IA /download/ needs a User-Agent and -L, is flaky per file, and zip-only Google-scan items have NO per-leaf image derivatives
Where: any fetch from archive.org (fit/src_numancia.py _ia_get/render, pipeline/books_ia.py); verified on item memoriasdelareal009real, 2026-10-12 (task 210)
Symptom: a GET /download/<item>/<file> without a UA returns 0 bytes; a HEAD without -L shows the 302 CDN redirect (normal); a GET on a per-leaf page image (/download/<item>/page/nNNNN.jpg) WITH a UA but WITHOUT -L also writes a 0-byte file (the 302 has an empty body - curl -sL + a browser UA is what works, verified 2026-10-14 on britanniaromanao00hors); some files serve a transient 170-byte nginx 500 HTML page that comes and go per file/day; on a zip-only Google-scan item, /download/<item>_NNN.jpg and .jp2, BookReaderImages.php and /composite/ all 404.
Why: the CDN wants a UA and follows redirects, and the /download/ backend fails intermittently per file - retry with backoff (the module tries 3x). A zip-only Google-scan item has no per-leaf image derivatives AT ALL: per-leaf images exist only inside the jp2.zip / orig tar, so per-leaf images come from the PDF (pdftoppm) or the zip, never from a per-leaf URL. When /download/page_numbers.json 500s, /metadata/<item> returns the page_numbers dict inline (its "pages" list has one {leafNum, ...} entry per leaf; files[].size values are STRINGS, e.g. "37664978").

#### In memoriasdelareal009real the OCR page index does not line up with the PDF leaf order - ground truth is the PDF
Where: IA item memoriasdelareal009real (RAH Memorias tomo IX, 1879); fit/src_numancia.py (LEAF = 507), docs/lead_numancia.md §2 leaf map
Symptom: the work that starts at PDF leaf 378 has its running heads at hOCR searchtext entries ~33-38; a leaf looked up through the OCR page index lands on the wrong leaf (same class as the civitatesorbiste00brau hOCR misalignment, different book).
Why: this scan's OCR page index / searchtext sequence does not match the PDF leaf sequence 1:1. Eye-check a leaf (pdftoppm render) before trusting its number; the plain djvu text stream does read in document order, so a whitespace-collapsed search for a known line (the plate's ÍNDICE line) is reliable for identification - all the module's sweep uses it for.

#### A staged row whose image has no fetchable URL needs a per-module re-render command, and its tests stay hermetic about the file
Where: fit/src_numancia.py (--render), tests/test_src_numancia.py; data/raw is a gitignored shared store (see the two data/raw entries above)
Symptom: the row's image exists only in the worktree where it was rendered; in every other checkout the local file is missing, so a test that asserts its existence fails there, and the page / export silently omits the row.
Why: data/raw/ never travels in git. When the source has no fetchable per-leaf image (IA zip-only scan), the staging module ships a --render command (download + pdftoppm into the sha1(title)[:16] slot) as the per-worktree re-derivation, and the tests check the path convention and validate the file only when present. The row carries no `thumb` (a thumb pointing at the source PDF would store the PDF as .jpg): commons.thumbs() skips it, tools/export_plans.py omits it in image-less worktrees, tools/fitkit.py plan_image raises only if that row is opened there.

#### This machine has /usr/bin/pdftoppm (poppler-utils), and its single-page JPEG render is byte-reproducible
Where: fit/src_numancia.py render(); the data/raw/commons/numancia/ plate
Symptom: none (a capability): `pdftoppm -jpeg -r 300 -jpegopt quality=85 -f N -l N -singlefile in.pdf out.jpg` produces one <prefix>.jpg (no page-number suffix with -singlefile) and the output is byte-identical across runs (memoriasdelareal009real leaf 507 -> sha256 c8415ffb94c6bfa50aea92335efef9e0babab8be615f7a44df2b55bfc9931415, 6713x2709, 1157133 bytes).
Why: pinning the render recipe keeps the per-worktree re-derivation identical, so the row's w/h and the sha1 file name stay stable across worktrees. Non-blank test: the grayscale histogram std (a real plate is tens; flat white/black JPEG q85 stand-ins 0.00; the module's threshold is 1.0).

#### A full-suite run writes ~3.5G into /tmp/loop-<project>; a disk-full run dies with misleading failures (Errno 28 in many tests, RemoteDisconnected in test_serve)
Where: the whole tests/ suite (tests/conftest.py's session-scoped fixtures - `served`, awline, `place_served` - each copy the tree into $TMPDIR, which on this machine is /tmp/loop-ancient-works.c); `df -h /`
Symptom: `OSError: [Errno 28] No space left on device` across many tests of one run; `http.client.RemoteDisconnected: Remote end closed connection without response` in tests/test_serve.py::test_document_store_roundtrip (the session server process died mid-request); `could not create numbered dir ... after 10 tries`. Seen 2026-10-12: the 48G disk was 95% full, the driver's 306c verification run hit exactly this and the done-claim was rejected - although the test logic is sound (it passes on a run with headroom).
Why: each session-fixture copy is ~1.2G (data/ 637M + web/ 524M + code) and a run makes three of them (aw0, awline0, awplace0) ≈ 3.5G; pytest keeps the last 3 numbered runs, so up to ~10G accumulates in /tmp/loop-<project>, and the other checkouts/projects on the same 48G disk add to it. Recipe: `df -h /` and `du -sh /tmp/loop-*` before and after a run; delete dead numbered dirs (≈3.5G each) when no pytest/chromium is running (`ps aux | grep -E "pytest|chrom"` - never touch another project's /tmp/loop-* dirs; as of 2026-10-12 the loop's own maintenance also wipes them, see next entry). A run that died on a full disk is environmental: clean and re-run before blaming the code.

#### The loop's maintenance wipes stale /tmp/loop-*/pytest-of-agent dirs when the disk nears full, and the driver's verification cycle kills competing in-flight runs in the checkout it verifies (a dead driver run orphans its servers)
Where: /tmp/loop-* of every checkout; .agent/reports/last-test-output.txt; `ps -eo pid,ppid,etime,args`
Symptom: another checkout's multi-G pytest dir vanishes on its own (agent a's: 7.0G at 2026-10-12 ~17:47, 2.3G at ~17:55 - no agent did it); your own full-suite run dies with exit 143 (SIGTERM) mid-run with no error in its own output; after a dead driver verification, PPID-1 orphan `server/serve.py --port 0` and hermetic `-c runpy ... server/serve.py` processes sit in the checkout, and .agent/reports/last-test-output.txt's mtime is older than the crash (a crashed driver run writes no report).
Why: the loop self-heals disk pressure by reclaiming dead numbered dirs, and preempts a checkout it is about to verify. Consequences: before starting a full-suite run check `ps -eo pid,ppid,etime,args | grep -E "pytest|serve.py|runpy"` for (a) live runs in other checkouts (their 3.5G writes race yours for the same 48G disk - two concurrent full runs need ~7G free) and (b) driver processes in THIS checkout (starting then gets your run killed, as at 2026-10-12 17:44, 5 min before the driver's 17:48-49 verification). PPID-1 orphan servers from a dead run are safe to `kill`; their dead numbered dirs safe to delete. A run with ≥4G headroom at start (3.5G write + margin) survives; one starting at <2G free dies with the Errno 28 cascade above.

#### The driver's done-claim verification budget was 900 s, set when the suite was ~249 s; the 307-family browser tests grew it to 642-1040 s green, so a green run reads as a "hang" and the claim is rejected (raised to 1800 s on 2026-10-15, AUTO-DECIDED request 004)
Where: the driver's done-claim verification (`.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q` after merging main into the branch); the rejection note in DECISIONS.md; `.agent/reports/last-test-output.txt`
Symptom: a done claim rejected with "The test suite did not finish within 900 s: a test hangs" though the identical command exits green in 642-1040 s; `last-test-output.txt` ends mid-progress-line with NO summary, and its mtime is start + exactly 900 s (a kill, not a crash - no OOM, memory healthy).
Why: the budget never moved since the 151-test / 249-s suite (2026-10-12, .agent/reports/iter199-suite.log); the 307-family headless-Chrome tests (owner check, matchfit_station, review, serve) took the time ~4x. Decode before hunting for a hang: a mid-progress-line ending plus an exact-900-s mtime delta is a budget kill. It was raised to 1800 s on 2026-10-15 (request 004, auto-decided at the 120-min default; DECISIONS it.252). If the suite outgrows ~1700 s, or a claim dies with this exact phrasing again, file ask_human for a new budget rather than assuming a test hang - and never "fix" it by deleting or shortening other tasks' tests (team mode forbids touching their files).

#### The Web-Mercator y-tile formula is y = ((1 - ln(tan φ + sec φ)/π)/2)·2^z - a misplaced /2 shifts by half the tile ring (Gulf-of-Guinea blanks)
Where: the 306d/306c audit scripts' tile fetchers (/tmp/j306d/j165c_tiles.py, /tmp/j306c/); any code that converts a lat/lon to a slippy-map tile
Symptom: the fetched tiles are blank ocean (the Gulf of Guinea) instead of the requested location - the y index is off by 0.5·2^z (at z15 London lands at y 13640 instead of 10897)
Why: writing (1 - ln(...)/(2π))·2^z (the /2 applied inside the parentheses) doubles the y fraction. Sanity check, verified by running it: London (0, 51.5) z15 = (16384, 10897); the x index is the simple (lon+180)/360·2^z.

#### ArcGIS online service names both start with 'World' - never name tile output files by a service prefix
Where: the 306d audit scripts fetching https://server.arcgisonline.com/.../World_Imagery and World_Topo_Map tiles (/tmp/j306d/j165c_tiles.py)
Symptom: the second service's fetch silently overwrote the first's files (both write 'cass15_wor_*.png' if named by svc[:3]), so a 'topo' composite was actually imagery - no error anywhere
Why: World_Imagery[:3] == World_Topo_Map[:3] == 'wor'. Name output files with a tag derived from the full service name ('imag'/'topo') or separate directories.

#### In a raw-tile composite, metres-per-pixel = (360/2^z · 111194.93 · cos lat)/256 - forgetting the /256 collapses every marker onto the site point
Where: the 306d marker composites (/tmp/j306d/j165e_compose.py); any overlay of ground-referenced markers on pasted slippy-map tiles
Symptom: markers that should be 300-450 m apart all sit 1-2 px from the centre, and the 200 m scale bar draws as a 1-px dot - the whole judge image looked like the fit was perfect while it was 256x too small (this masked the cassiobury miss on the first 165 read)
Why: 360/2^z is one TILE's lon span (256 px), not one pixel's; mpp = that product / 256 (0.74 at z17/51.7°, 3.0 at z15). Equivalently: a pixel offset computed as metres/tile-span needs *256.

#### Overpass is dead from this VM on all public instances (406/504/XHTML) - use the regular OSM API: /map?bbox (<=0.02x0.02 deg) and /api/0.6/{node,way,relation}/{id}/full with a browser UA, retested per call; Nominatim /search (project UA, 1 r/s) for ID lookups, but its /geojson gives only a centroid Point for big rivers
Where: the 306d/306c OSM context queries (/tmp/j306d/j165d_osm.py, j166_osm.py) and the 236a Nashville confluence work (163/164); overpass-api.de, overpass.kumi.systems, maps.mail.ru:8080, api.openstreetmap.org, nominatim.openstreetmap.org
Symptom: overpass-api.de answers 406 (it 504'd / 400'd in the 306d era), maps.mail.ru 504, kumi an XHTML error page instead of JSON (2026-10-13, three hosts, repeated attempts) - yet the regular API is alive: GET api.openstreetmap.org /map?bbox=... and /api/0.6/way/40806685/full return 200 with data (2026-10-14, browser UA). The states flip between days, so retest per call, never assume.
Why: the public overpass cluster is overloaded/rate-limits this VM's traffic; the regular cgit API has much higher per-endpoint limits. Recipe that works: (a) Nominatim /search?q=<name>&format=json with the project UA at 1 r/s to get OSM object IDs; (b) GET /api/0.6/{node,way,relation}/{id}/full for the full geometry (browser UA); (c) GET /map?bbox=minlat,minlon,maxlat,maxlon with a browser UA, box <= ~0.02x0.02 deg (the response is limited to ~400 nodes - a bigger box 400s). Caveat: Nominatim /geojson for a big RIVER returns only a centroid Point, not the course (Tennessee relation 2182503 gave the Blytheville terminus point, 163) - fetch the relation and walk its main_stream ways through the API instead.

#### `memoirwrittendur0000henr` is NOT the Maclauchlan 1971 reprint - it is Linda Nochlin's *Realism* (1971)
Where: IA item memoirwrittendur0000henr (the "1971 reprint" candidate for Maclauchlan's survey of the Roman Wall, task 207b); data/raw/books/memoirwrittendur0000henr/ (cached metadata/bookreader)
Symptom: the item's IA title says the Maclauchlan memoir, but the page content is a different book (Nochlin, *Realism*); its hOCR text never matches the survey's front matter, so a list transcribed from it would be transcribing the wrong book
Why: IA item re-scan/mislabel (the item was re-scanned 2024-01-31) - the item's title and its page content disagree. Never use this item as an OCR source for the Maclauchlan list. The 1858 original's own djvu.xml carries enough text: the book's only list is the DIRECTIONS TO THE BINDER on djvu leaf 119 (see next entry), and per-leaf OCR comes from the djvu.xml OBJECTs (no hOCR page index on the 1858 original).

#### The Maclauchlan 1858 original has NO printed plate list - the binder's instructions are the book's list
Where: IA item memoirwrittendu00maclgoog (1858 original, 171 leaves); djvu leaf 119 (the DIRECTIONS TO THE BINDER page); fit/src_roman_maclauchlan.py; data/books/triage/memoirwrittendu00maclgoog.A.jsonl
Symptom: a search for a LIST / PLATES / CONTENTS heading in the front and back matter finds nothing; the plate leaves carry only their own printed "FIG. n" numbers, so there is no list page to OCR-map
Why: the privately-circulated 1858 original was never given a plate list; the binder's page (djvu leaf 119) is the only one - transcribe it by eye into the books_lists HAND_FIGS table (the 207a/Horsley pattern), no OCR-based list exists. Verbatim: "The Plans, Fig. 1, 2, 3, and 6, showing the Mote, Brampton, &c., to be inserted at page 65. The Plans, &c. of the Roman Wall in Willow Holm, at page 76. The Plans, Fig. 4, 6, Carlisle and the Camp on Skew Hill at page 76." Exactly three small-format plate leaves (n0078 Fig. 1 Brampton, n0090 Willow Holm wall plan/section, n0093 Fig. 4 Carlisle; triage 964x1400); n0111 (p.93, the 1856 Housesteads gateway figure) and n0115 (p.97, Table of Stations) are quarto text pages (964x1400) with inline figures, and n0129 is a full-size (890x1400) text page - none of those three is a plate leaf; Figs 2, 3 and 5/6 were never printed in this copy. Figs 1 and the gateway figure are BLANK in this copy (the drawing faded; only frame/labels/scale bar remain) - read the IMAGES (bookreader leafNum) for plate identity, the djvu leaves are aligned 1:1 here but two leaves (n0089, n0095) are genuine blanks a text-based mapping could misassign.

## Libraries and frameworks

One `### <library>` subsection per library or tool, with its version.

### pillow (12.3.0, project .venv)

#### A Float32 DEM (the Dutch AHN) needs the `imagecodecs` package - without it every AHN-sourced site fails to build
Where: pipeline/build_site.py:load_dem -> aw.fetch_dem -> dem_sources._read_geotiff (tifffile on the AHN WCS bytes; the FLOATINGPOINT predictor is decoded via Pillow), the `.venv` build from requirements.txt
Symptom: `ValueError: <PREDICTOR.FLOATINGPOINT: 3> requires the 'imagecodecs' package` at build time; the AHN-sourced sites (amsterdam-q727, alkmaar-q972, enkhuizen-q9918, haarlem-q9920, rotterdam-q34370, the-hague-q36600, utrecht-q803) all fail, while the point-cloud fallback saves only the boxes pc covers (reimerswaal, sluis, valkenburg)
Why: AHN DEMs ship as Float32 rasters and Pillow cannot decode that predictor without imagecodecs (reproduced 2026-10-13 in a scratch venv with pillow+tifffile only: one AHN tile fails with exactly this error). It is now pinned in requirements.in as imagecodecs==2026.10.10 (229) and lands in every venv built from requirements.txt, including from scratch: 2026-10-13 a fresh venv from the regenerated file fetched and decoded the full utrecht-q803 2000x2000 box (1.00 share, matching the cached dem.npy to 0.000 m).
What to do: on this exact error, imagecodecs has gone missing from the venv (a requirements.txt regeneration dropped the pin, or the venv predates 229): regenerate requirements.txt from requirements.in (pip-compile --generate-hashes from a throwaway venv, the 800 recipe) and rebuild the venv. Do not bump past 2026.10.10 without re-verifying an AHN build.

### pyproj (3.8, project .venv)

#### `pyproj.CRS("OSGB36")` is NOT the British National Grid, and EPSG:4326's authority axis order is (lat, lon)
Where: any OSGB36/BNG to WGS84 conversion (task 205's Kings Weston grid-ref check); `pyproj.Transformer.from_crs`
Symptom: `Transformer.from_crs("OSGB36", "WGS84").transform(352900, 177100)` returns (51.490873, -2.679790) with
      the two VALUES SWAPPED in meaning (x=lat, y=lon) - and with a plain geographic name like "OSGB36" the
      transform degrades toward a pass-through (the first attempt returned the inputs essentially unchanged). A
      default Transformer TO EPSG:4326 emits (lat, lon), because 4326's authority axis order is lat, lon.
Why: the projected British National Grid is EPSG:27700; "OSGB36" is the datum's geographic system. Use
      `pyproj.Transformer.from_crs('EPSG:27700', 'EPSG:4326', always_xy=True)` and read the result as
      (lon, lat). Verified 2026-10-13, both directions: BNG (352900, 177100) -> (lon -2.679790, lat 51.490873)
      near SW Bristol; Bristol centre (51.4545, -2.5879) -> (359247, 173000) = ST5927, the well-known centre of
      Bristol.

#### A 6-figure OS grid ref's digits are relative to its 100 km square's origin - the ST square is (300000, 100000), not (400000, 700000)
Where: any decoding of a UK 6-figure grid ref before a pyproj conversion (e.g. the enwiki
      `{{gbmapping|ST529771}}` on the Kings Weston House page; task 205)
Symptom: decoding the digits as (400000 + 52900, 700000 + 77100) and converting to WGS84 lands near (-1.13,
      56.88) - the Scottish border, ~600 km from Bristol.
Why: the three digit-pairs are 100 m offsets from the 100 km square's OWN origin; each square has a different
      origin (TQ = 400000/100000 - that is why Greenwich is TQ3280; S is one easting square west of T, so
      ST = 300000/100000). Verified 2026-10-13 by the round-trip: ST529771 = (352900, 177100) -> (51.490873,
      -2.679790), SW Bristol, which converts back to exactly (352900, 177100). Note this also means a grid ref in
      an enwiki article can disagree with the article's infobox coordinates (Kings Weston House: 1.3 km) -
      cross-check both against Nominatim/OSM before quoting either.
### Python (3.12.3)

#### A trailing comment after a complete expression inside an unbalanced-bracket display does not end the logical line
Where: any multi-line dict/list literal (hit in fit/src_van_deventer.py's TOWNS: a `"Sluis": dict(...)` entry
      whose last line read `p373="Sluis")  # the name search` - the comma was missing)
Symptom: `SyntaxError: invalid syntax. Perhaps you forgot a comma?` reported at the NEXT key's line, several
      lines below where the comma is actually missing (the comment hid it)
Why: inside `{...}`/`[...]` physical lines are joined into one logical line until the brackets balance; a
      trailing comment on a bracket-balanced line does not end that logical line, so the next physical line
      gets glued on and the following `key: value` lands where a comma was expected. Put comments INSIDE the
      parentheses, or after the closing `),` - never after a `)` whose comma you might have dropped.

#### dict.update() of a list of 2-tuples builds {first: second}, not a {key: [values]} mapping
Where: fit/src_van_deventer.py (verify_qids candidate collection - the shape was wrong there once; the trap
      stays for anyone rebuilding a town -> [candidates] map)
Symptom: expecting {town: [candidates]} and getting {qid: label}; the next unpack crashes with "too many
      values to unpack"
Why: update() treats an iterable of 2-element sequences as (key, value) pairs. To collect values per key,
      accumulate explicitly: `d.setdefault(key, []).append(item)` - never `d.update(pairs)` for that shape.

#### In a generator expression `for r in files and cond` binds the `and` to the ITERABLE
Where: `fit/src_van_deventer.py`'s `golden()` (crashed at `--golden`, fixed iter 56); any
      `any(... for x in LIST and x.attr in SET)` pattern
Symptom: `UnboundLocalError: cannot access local variable 'r' where it is not associated with a value` -
      the expression parses as `for r in (files and r.get("title") in ...)`, so the iterable itself
      references `r` before the loop binds it.
Why: in a generator expression the text after the first `for <name> in <expr>` is the FILTER test; the
      iterable `<expr>` must not reference the loop variable. Write the conjunction inside the body:
      `any(r.get("site") == s["id"] and r.get("title") in picked for r in files)`.

#### Replacing `socket.socket` with a function breaks a later `ssl` import - import `urllib.request`/`ssl` first, then patch the connect methods
Where: ad-hoc offline verification runs (207a iteration 219's --list socket-block wrapper); the in-test in-process
      pattern is tests/test_batch_us.py's `no_network` fixture
Symptom: `socket.socket = fn` followed by any import chain that reaches `import ssl` dies with
      `TypeError: function() argument 'code' must be code, not str` (in `class SSLSocket(socket.socket)`) -
      an stdlib crash that looks unrelated to the patch
Why: `ssl` subclasses `socket.socket` at import time, so the attribute must still be a class by the time
      ssl is imported. To prove a command path is offline: `import urllib.request, ssl` FIRST, then
      `socket.socket.connect = dead` and `socket.create_connection = dead`, then run the script (urlopen and
      http.client both funnel through those two; DNS never runs because connect raises first).

#### A monkeypatched socket in the parent process never reaches a subprocess - guard the subprocess itself with `python -c` + runpy (and there sys.argv[0] == "-c")
Where: tests that run the product's CLI as a subprocess (tests/test_site_done.py's GUARD); the in-process pattern
      is tests/test_batch_us.py's `no_network` fixture
Symptom: `monkeypatch.setattr(socket.socket, "connect", dead)` in the pytest process does nothing to a child
      spawned afterwards (separate interpreter, fresh socket module) - the child can hit the network, so the
      "hermetic" test is not hermetic (no loud failure, just a download).
Why: patches are per-process. Run the child as `[sys.executable, "-c", GUARD, script, *args]` where GUARD
      patches `socket.socket.connect`/`connect_ex` and `socket.create_connection` to raise, then
      `runpy.run_path(script, run_name="__main__")` - the script's own `__main__` block runs with `__file__`
      set, so a module that derives its data root from its own path runs on the intended tree. Two gotchas:
      in a `-c` process `sys.argv[0]` is the literal string "-c" (the real arguments start at argv[1]); and
      pass `PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8` in the child's env so non-ASCII output (em-dashes in Commons titles)
      cannot crash it or the decoding under a non-UTF-8 locale.

#### runpy.run_path does not put the script's own directory on sys.path - a tool script importing a sibling must insert it itself
Where: tools/fit_queue.py (the 804 wiring imports tools/right_place.py and fit/review.py); every test GUARD that runs a tools/*.py script via runpy (tests/test_fit_queue.py, test_site_done.py, test_fit_provenance.py)
Symptom: `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'right_place'` when the tool runs under the test's runpy guard, although the same script works as `python3 tools/fit_queue.py` on the Mac
Why: a plain `python3 <script>` sets sys.path[0] to the script's directory; `runpy.run_path` (the guard's runner) does not. The guard process starts from the checkout root, so neither the tools/ nor the fit/ directory is importable. Insert the needed directories into sys.path inside the script before the import (tools/right_place.py's main() already does this for fit_queue - the wiring does the same for right_place and fit/review).

#### Path.glob yields files in filesystem order, not sorted order
Where: any test that asserts on the sequence of a `glob`/`iterdir` result (hit in tests/test_fit_queue.py's
      namesake test: two item files compared against a hand-written sorted list)
Symptom: an order-sensitive assertion (`list(...) == ["a.json", "b.json"]`) passes on one machine and fails on
      another with the names swapped - `Path.glob` iterates `os.scandir` in directory order, which is
      unspecified and filesystem-dependent
Why: never rely on glob order: sort the results (`for p in sorted(dir.glob("*.json"))`) before any
      order-sensitive comparison; a dict built from an unsorted glob carries that order into `list(dict)`,
      so sort at the glob, not at the assert.

### scipy (1.18.1, project .venv)

#### scipy 1.18's ndi.center_of_mass with a label-index array returns one (cy, cx) tuple per label, not (cy_arr, cx_arr)
Where: `tests/test_surveyfit.py` (`_centroids`), `fit/surveyfit.py` (`panel_pieces` - it uses the single-mask form there)
Symptom: `cy, cx = ndi.center_of_mass(ink, lab, np.arange(1, n + 1))` raises "ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 2)" whenever n != 2
Why: the labelled form returns a list of (cy, cx) tuples, one per label. The single-mask form `ndi.center_of_mass(m)` still returns one (cy, cx) tuple. Unpack with `[(c[1], c[0]) for c in com]`. The version is pinned in requirements.txt - do not write defensive code for other scipy versions.

#### ndi.shift's shift sequence must match the array's rank - an RGB image (h, w, 3) needs a 3-element shift
Where: `fit/surveyfit.py` (`shift_sheet_image` - the 302b sheet-shift null applied to the loaded sheet image, which is always RGB)
Symptom: "RuntimeError: sequence argument must have length equal to input rank" when shifting with `shift=(-h*f, w*f)`
Why: ndi.shift checks len(shift) == input.ndim; a 2-element shift only fits 2-D arrays. The null path had never been executed (the early stub tests use null=False), so the crash surfaced at the first null run. Fix: `shift=(-h*f, w*f, 0.0)`.
#### select() on a coprocess pipe's fd is not a wait for more LINES when you read through Python's buffered reader
Where: tests that pump a server's stdout (tests/test_fit_queue.py part 2 - the drain loop timed out for a
      line that was already delivered; the coprocess was read as `subprocess.Popen(..., text=True)` and
      consumed with `select.select([proc.stdout.fileno()], ...)` + `proc.stdout.readline()`)
Symptom: the drain loop sees only the first few lines (whatever the first readline() pre-fetched), then
      `select` never reports the fd ready again - even though the coprocess prints more lines seconds later
      and the "missing" burst appears only after EOF (killing the process made the whole tail arrive at once).
Why: a readline() on a TextIOWrapper pulls a big raw chunk (up to 16 KB) from the OS pipe into its internal
      buffer; the fd then reads as empty, so select() no longer reflects data that still waits in the Python
      buffer, and data landing in the pipe in the meantime can go unreported between select() calls. There
      was no hang in the coprocess at all (a raw `os.read` reader thread showed the whole run finishing in
      23 s; one run additionally showed a whole-process stall of minutes under parallel-agent load - its
      watchdog `time.sleep(60)` never woke - so keep the test's deadline well beyond the measured runtime).
What to do: drain coprocess output in a dedicated thread that does plain blocking reads (`for line in
      proc.stdout:` or `os.read` in a loop) into a list the test polls; never combine select() with a
      buffered reader on the same fd.

### PIL (12.3.0, project .venv)

#### PIL is in the project .venv only (pinned in requirements as `pillow`), never in system python3
Where: plate-image measurement (scale bars, figure crops) in audit work; `.venv`
Symptom: `python3 -c "import PIL"` -> ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'PIL' while `.venv/bin/python -c "import PIL"` works (12.3.0)
Why: PIL came in via requirements.in (`pillow`, pinned `pillow==12.3.0` in requirements.txt) for the 306 audit's scale-bar measurements. Run any image measurement with `.venv/bin/python`; the driver's venv rebuild already carries it.
### pytest (9.1.1, project .venv)

#### Two pytest sessions of one checkout trash each other's temp trees: a session that ends green rmtree's the WHOLE basetemp, so a suite left running past its session gets destroyed
Where: every pytest run in this checkout (the harness sets `TMPDIR=/tmp/loop-<checkout-dir>` for all processes, and pytest 9.1.1's default basetemp is `$TMPDIR/pytest-of-<user>` - ONE directory shared by all sessions of the checkout); pytest.ini (`tmp_path_retention_count=1`, `tmp_path_retention_policy=failed`); tests/conftest.py's session-scoped `served` fixture; tests/test_serve.py, tests/test_review.py
Symptom: a suite left in the background (nohup'd, outliving its session) fails with `urllib.error.HTTPError: HTTP Error 404` in test_serve on the served `/` and `FileNotFoundError` in test_review for files of its OWN tree's data/review/ that exist in the checkout, while a run of the same tree minutes earlier was green; the leftover temp tree (.../pytest-of-agent/pytest-N/aw0) is near-empty (web/ and server/ gone, only directories the tests recreated after the deletion remain). (Observed 2026-10-13, task 308: a nohup'd full suite lost its tree ~80 s in; the 00:40 run of the same tree had passed those tests, and an in-session re-run was green apart from the known 231/232 reds. The exact concurrent run that did it could not be identified - its process was gone - but the mechanism below is from pytest 9.1.1's own source.)
Why: at session end pytest (a) rmtree's the entire basetemp root when the session ended green with the "failed" policy and no explicit --basetemp, and (b) the numbered-dir cleanup (keep=1) removes older `pytest-N` directories - both act on directories of OTHER still-running sessions that share the TMPDIR-derived basetemp.
How to avoid: run the full suite in the FOREGROUND of your session (a plain `&`, not nohup - it then dies with the session, so it can never outlive it), and never start a second pytest run in this checkout while one is running (the driver's suite runs happen at iteration boundaries, which is when a leftover run gets destroyed). If a run you left behind fails with this signature, re-run the suite in-session before blaming the code: compare with the last clean run of the same tree.

#### `-o tmp_path_retention_policy=all` does NOT keep previous run dirs: the pytest.ini count=1 (mirrored in the driver's PYTEST_ADDOPTS) still prunes everything but the newest pytest-N, because every session unlinks its own cleanup lock at exit
Where: every pytest run in this project - pytest.ini (`tmp_path_retention_count = 1`, `tmp_path_retention_policy = failed`) plus the driver's agent-loop exporting the same two into PYTEST_ADDOPTS for all session children; pytest 9.1.1 `_pytest/tmpdir.py` (`keep = retention_count` for "all" and "failed" alike, only "none" sets 0) and `_pytest/pathlib.py` (`cleanup_candidates`: dirs numbered <= max_existing-keep; `ensure_deletable`: deletable when the lock file is missing or older than the 3-day timeout)
Symptom: after consecutive green pytest invocations with `-o tmp_path_retention_policy=all`, $TMPDIR/pytest-of-agent/ holds only the LATEST `pytest-<N>` dir (plus the `pytest-current` symlink) - measured 2026-10-15 (iteration 214, agent c, task 245): three owner_check pair runs left only pytest-2; a 4-run dummy loop left one dir per run; adding `-o tmp_path_retention_count=10` made all accumulate (9,10,11,12) and the stale ones died exactly per the keep arithmetic
Why: the policy knob only gates the green-run whole-basetemp rmtree (the "failed" branch of `pytest_sessionfinish`); the numbered-dir cleanup always runs with `keep = retention_count`, and each session unlinks its own lock at exit (LIFO exit-stack callback), so the NEXT session's cleanup finds every older dir lock-less and deletes it - the 3-day lock timeout never comes into play for back-to-back runs
What to do: for cross-run artifact comparison (e.g. a PIL diff of two pair runs) pass BOTH `-o tmp_path_retention_policy=all` AND `-o tmp_path_retention_count=N` (N >= the runs you want) - or copy each run's artifacts out to a lane dir WHILE the run is alive (see the next entry: a green run deletes its basetemp before the process exits, so "right after the run" is already too late); a post-hoc compare from $TMPDIR/pytest-of-agent only ever sees the latest run

#### A green run deletes its whole basetemp BEFORE the process exits (pytest_sessionfinish), so a post-invocation copy of its artifacts finds nothing; `-o tmp_path_retention_count=N` alone does not stop the delete - only `policy == "failed"` and an explicit `--basetemp` gate it
Where: any green pytest run in this checkout - pytest 9.1.1 `_pytest/tmpdir.py::pytest_sessionfinish` (`if exitstatus == 0 and policy == "failed" and tmp_path_factory._given_basetemp is None: rmtree(basetemp, ignore_errors=True)` - verified from the .venv source 2026-10-15, iteration 255) and `::get_basetemp` (an explicit `--basetemp` bypasses the numbered-dir/keep mechanism entirely: no pruning, no exit-stack cleanup on that root); pytest.ini's `tmp_path_retention_policy = failed` (mirrored in the driver's PYTEST_ADDOPTS) keeps the rmtree armed on every plain invocation
Symptom: `pytest <...> && cp $TMPDIR/pytest-of-agent/... <lane>/` in one command chain copies nothing even though the run just wrote the files seconds earlier (2026-10-15 246: the pair run's ten views + probe logs per run were gone by the time the shell chain reached the cp; the "wiped before the first ls after exit" symptom of the test_owner_check probe-logs entry is the same mechanism)
Why: sessionfinish runs INSIDE the pytest process, before exit; its rmtree condition does not include retention_count (that only sets `keep=` for the numbered-dir pruning), so `-o tmp_path_retention_count=2` (the recipe the 246 task Notes originally suggested) leaves a green run wiped exactly as before. Two working alternatives: (a) the PAIR `-o tmp_path_retention_policy=all -o tmp_path_retention_count=N` (policy "all" removes the rmtree; the count then fully controls the numbered-dir retention - the previous entry measured it), or (b) an explicit `--basetemp=<dir>` (no numbered dirs, no root rmtree; per-test `tmp_path` dirs of passing tests still get individually removed under policy "failed", but module/session-scoped `tmp_path_factory.mktemp` trees - the owner_check ownerA0/ownerB0 views and awowner0 private tree - survive)
What to do: when the recorded command must stay bare (a task pins the exact invocation, like 246's), copy artifacts out of the basetemp WHILE the run is alive: a 0.1 s os.walk watcher process started BEFORE pytest (fresh process per run, its own dest dir, flattened relpath keys, re-copy on size/mtime change, stop-file + grace sweeps - the 814/816 recipe widened from the probe log to the PNGs; the 246 it.255 lane $TMPDIR/owner-xrun/run{k}/). The lane lives in the checkout's own /tmp/loop-<checkout> TMPDIR (a sibling of pytest-of-agent, so the loop's /tmp/loop-*/pytest-of-agent wiper leaves it alone DURING the session) but dies with the session-boundary recreation of /tmp/loop-<checkout> - record the numbers in DECISIONS in the same session that made them

#### test_review::test_page_shows_the_review_list reds intermittently when an external Esri tile fetch fails: the probe asserts ZERO [reqfail] lines while its owner_check sibling treats the same in-flight aborts as normal - a transient network red, not a code regression
Where: tests/test_review.py::test_page_shows_the_review_list (headless node shot.mjs probe of the review page; the page's MapLibre basemap fetches https://server.arcgisonline.com/ArcGIS/rest/services/World_Imagery/MapServer/tile/...), its sibling tests/test_owner_check.py (same fetches; the tests/playwright entry above records its [reqfail] ERR_ABORTED lines as "normal in-flight aborts on this machine")
Symptom: `AssertionError: assert '[reqfail]' not in '[console] w...'` with `[reqfail] https://server.arcgisonline.com/.../tile/... net::ERR_FAILED` + `[console] error Failed to fetch (0)` (2026-10-14, 241 iteration 174: one full run red, an isolated re-run 31 s later green while a direct urllib fetch of the same tile returned 200/7511 B)
Why/fix: this machine's egress to arcgisonline.com is intermittent (Wikimedia is reachable, loc.gov 403s, Esri neither pinned nor blocked), and this test is the strictest reader of the [reqfail] lines (zero tolerated) of the tests that share the basemap. A red here on otherwise-green code = network flake: re-run the single test (~30 s) and check the tile with a one-line urllib fetch before suspecting anything in web/ or the page.

## This codebase

One `### <module or service>` subsection per part of this project. Say in `Where:` which other parts depend on it:
a trap in one part often shows up in another.

#### books_match `name_keys` strips descriptors only from already-normalized (lowercase) names
Where: `pipeline/books_match.py` (`SUFFIX`, `name_keys`; its own callers `load_catalog` and `phrases`/`match_row`),
      `fit/evidence.py` (`check_book_caption`)
Symptom: passing a raw name ("Fort Hill State Memorial") to `name_keys` returns the one-element set {that
      name} - the " State Memorial" suffix survives, so a substring test against normalized row text
      ("fort hill") fails: "the row does not name 'Fort Hill State Memorial'" on a row that plainly does.
Why: `SUFFIX` is a case-sensitive regex over lowercase forms, and every call site inside books_match
      normalizes first, so the convention is invisible from inside the module. Outside callers must do the
      same: `name_keys(re.sub(r"\s+", " ", norm(name)).strip())`, then test keys against normalized text.

#### `web/data/sites.json`: the only universal keys are id/name/lon/lat/corners/size_m/drawings
Where: `web/data/sites.json`, `tests/test_serve.py`, the batch tasks (203a/203b)
Symptom: a test or tool that requires `place`, `kind`, `qid` or `region` fails for some sites: of the 384,
6 have no `region`, 48 no `qid`, 33 no `wiki`.
Why: entries are written by `build_site.py` from partially filled catalog rows. Assert only the seven
universal keys; select US sites with `region == "US"` (90 of 384) and treat all the rest (294, including
the 6 without a region) as "non-US" so none is skipped by a batch or a test.

#### `web/data/plans.json` rows may share an `id` - one row per depicted site, per-site url
Where: `web/data/plans.json`, `web/index.html` (`P.byId`), `tools/export_plans.py`, test row lookups
Symptom: code that resolves a plan by id through a dict gets the wrong site's row: two rows share
the id (one per depicted site) and carry a DIFFERENT url/media path per site, so `rows_by_id[plan]`
returns site A's row when the entry belongs to site B (hit by tests/test_batch_eu.py, which then
asserted the stonehenge url against the avebury entry). The true key is `(id, sites[0])`; look up a
row per site from the site's own candidate list. As of the plan two pairs share an id: "The new
Larned History..." (avebury-q661855 + stonehenge-q39671) and "File:Mayburgh-1769.png"
(mayburgh-henge + king-arthur-s-round-table). The page's `P.byId` keeps only the last of the shared-
`id` rows; the fit-tool keying fix is scoped into 201.

#### `web/data/sites.json` and `web/data/plans.json` are dicts at the top level, not arrays
Where: `web/data/sites.json` ({"sites": [...]}), `web/data/plans.json` ({"cols": [...], "rows": [...]}); any script that counts or iterates their entries
Symptom: `len(json.load(open("web/data/plans.json")))` returns 2 (and sites.json 1) instead of the entry count - a "the file lost its rows" check fires on an intact file
Why: the serving machinery wraps the list: sites.json keeps the site array under "sites"; plans.json is the columnar cols/rows export written by tools/export_plans.py. Index into the wrapper before counting or iterating (verified 2026-10-12, iteration 190: 499 sites / 1,168 rows).

#### `serve.py` runs the plan_fit sync only after a platefits write, never at startup
Where: `server/serve.py` (`after_write`), `pipeline/plan_fit.py`
Symptom: (a safety fact, not an error) a GET-only test server never rebuilds site overlays; a
PUT/DELETE to `/api/db/platefits/*` wakes a worker thread that runs `plan_fit.main()` (it syncs all fits)
and the page polls `depictions.json` for the result.
Why: `after_write()` wakes the worker only for the `platefits` collection (its comment records that a
subprocess launched from the server silently died). GET-only tests are therefore safe and offline; a test
that PUTs a platefit should poll the site's `depictions.json`, not run `plan_fit` itself.

#### Composing a rotated/scaled Web-Mercator similarity about a centroid needs the full `a*w + b`, not just `a`
Where: `pipeline/plan_fit.py` (`similarity`), `pipeline/fit_gate.py` (`placement`), anything that derives a
wrong-placement variant of a fit (spike 7, `tools/gate_heldout.py`)
Symptom: a 10 deg turn or 15% scale about the placement centroid built as (a', b') =
(s*e^(iθ)*a, (1 - s*e^(iθ))*C_m) puts every anchor kilometres away (residuals ~4e6 m, gate kills the case
for the wrong reason, and a per-case pattern like the 0.1745 rot10 slope floor no longer appears).
Why: T'(w) = C + s*e^(iθ)*(T(w) - C) expands to s*e^(iθ)*T(w) + (1 - s*e^(iθ))*C, so b' must carry the
transformed b, b' = s*e^(iθ)*b + (1 - s*e^(iθ))*C_m (C_m = C/k in Mercator metres; C the placement's ground
centroid). The short form is only right when b = 0 (anchor centroid at the origin). The five verified
recipes (they reproduce docs/gate.md section 5 exactly): true (a, b); moved (a, b + d/k); rot10
(e^(i10°)*a, e^(i10°)*b + (1 - e^(i10°))*C_m); scale15 (1.15*a, 1.15*b - 0.15*C_m); xsite (a, b + (C_next - C)/k).

#### fit_gate cannot reject a 15% scale error at n = 3-6 anchors - a structural limit, not a bug
Where: `pipeline/fit_gate.py`, `tools/gate_heldout.py`, `docs/gate.md` sections 7 and 9
Symptom: the gate ACCEPTS scale15 placements: dev 2/12 (castle-rising, whitley), held-out 4/8
(avebury, badbury-rings, camp-d-attila, old-sarum n0142) - slope_o 0.130-0.144, all under the
frozen 0.145, none deep enough for the io < -10 clause.
Why: the theoretical 0.15*rho slope is attenuated by anchor noise in a through-origin fit at
n = 3-6 (dev band 0.130-0.141, held-out band 0.131-0.144 - the same band on both sets, so it
is not a threshold accident), and the residual pattern of a 15% scale sits inside a true
fit's own scatter: no pure-geometry statistic of these anchors can tell them apart. Do not
re-tune on the dev/held-out documents (the registration in docs/gate.md section 1 is void if
the frozen constants change) and do not add a scale-specific clause trained on this data.
Accept the 1-in-8 scale-error acceptance, backstopped by the review queue (GOAL 1) and the
human's 18/20 sample of auto-accepted fits (GOAL 3); a tighter rule may only be derived on
fresh documents with a fresh seed.

#### A transform=None gate cannot see a scale-shaped ground error of any measured magnitude - a 15%-scale matcher answer re-solves to median ~ 0
Where: `pipeline/fit_gate.py` (`gate`/`placement` with `transform=None`), `fit/batch_us.py`
      (`gate_placement`), `fit/matchfit.py` (`_settle`), the fails-gate test case of tasks/238-matcher-gate.md
Symptom: the variant the 238 task Notes proposed as the fails-gate matcher example (the pairs'
      ground points scaled 1.15x about their centroid, then `gate(pairs, None)`) does not fail:
      it ACCEPTS with med 0.0104 (a uniform 1.15x); a radial 15%/50% variant ACCEPTS too (med
      2.27/7.59) - a fails-gate test case built on scale silently passes.
Why: with transform=None the gate solves the canonical similarity from the pairs themselves, so a
      CONSISTENT global distortion (uniform or radial scale) is absorbed into the solved placement
      and the residuals return to ~0 (the section-7 limit, docs/gate.md). Only anchor-offset
      patterns fail it (4 of 8 anchors +-200 m E, alternating: med 96.8 m > 45 m, the median
      clause; 2 of 8: the slope clause) - i.e. what is self-inconsistent, measured. Section 9's
      scale15 rows were caught only because they were CLAIMED placements (transform != None) tested
      against recorded anchors. Build fails-gate test cases from anchor offsets and label them
      synthetic; the scale-shaped variants belong in the test as PASSING (they back the
      section-7 limit statement).

#### In-place re-dump of a jsonl line must carry the line terminator or rows glue together
Where: `fit/evidence.py` (`set_field`, `rewrite`, `record`); the test that guards it: `tests/test_evidence.py` (`test_record_appends_evidence_without_touching_existing_bytes`)
Symptom: after a `record`-style rewrite, one line of a jsonl file contains two JSON objects (this line
plus the next), the line count looks normal, and parsing the line as one object fails.
Why: `json.dumps` never emits a trailing newline, and a writer that replaces whole lines (readlines +
writelines) glues the next row onto the re-dumped one. `set_field` now appends `"\n"` iff the input line
had one. Any new in-place re-dump of a line-oriented file must do the same; verify with a per-line
parse + line-count + terminator check after the write.

#### The book matcher injects the book's default state and ties rows by token / exact-phrase lookup, never by full-name substring
Where: `pipeline/books_match.py` (`BOOK_SCOPE`, `row_inputs`, `score_candidate`, `match_row`), `fit/evidence.py` (`check_book_caption`)
Symptom: a re-verification of the matcher's own stored decisions FAILs matched rows with "stored place
state='ohio' recomputes to None" or "the row does not name 'Small multivallate hillfort on Pulpit Hill'"
(52 of the 135 matched book rows, found when 200 ran check on the real index).
Why: `match_row`'s place includes the BOOK_SCOPE default state (lapham_1855 wisconsin; fowke_1902 /
whittlesey_1850 / mills_1914 ohio; squier_1851 new york) when the printed text names none, and it ties a
row to a site by distinctive-token sharing or an exact phrase/alias lookup - the site's full name is
rarely printed (a title printing "Pulpit Hill" ties the site whose name is "Small multivallate hillfort on
Pulpit Hill"). Any consumer that re-verifies matcher decisions must call the matcher's own extracted
rules (`row_inputs` + `score_candidate`), never a stricter restatement of them.

#### The matcher's full output is non-monotone in catalog growth - never golden-pin it against the growing files
Where: `pipeline/books_match.py` (`main`, `match_row`), `data/books/matches.jsonl` (tracked), tasks 204-211 (they grow `data/books/index.jsonl` and the catalog)
Symptom: a persistent golden over `matches.jsonl` or the per-book status counts breaks when another task
merges new catalog sites or book rows (a new site can take the runner-up margin and flip matched -> ambiguous).
Why: the margin is a property of the whole candidate pool, not of one pair. To prove a matcher refactor
behavior-neutral, do a one-off before/after run and byte-compare (`matches.jsonl` hash + printed summary),
as 200 did. The evidence check deliberately stores the runner-up margin and does not re-run the matcher
over the catalog.

#### The catalog castrum-levefanum-q1309559 is the DUTCH Limes fort (5.35E 51.96N), not Beauvais (1.99E 49.42N)
Where: `data/catalog/sites.jsonl` (castrum-levefanum-q1309559); every distance computation or site identification
      that could fall back to a name-based guess
Symptom: assuming the site sits at Le Fanu/Beauvais (France) puts a sheet 314-368 km off; the stored point is
      the Dutch Lower Germanic Limes identification (region netherlands, part_of Q1265889).
Why: the name does not carry the geography - the catalog records the Dutch identification of the Roman
      Levefanum/Casaromago printed on the Peutinger map. Use the catalog's stored lon/lat, never a guess from
      the name (found task 801, iteration 17: the "Peutinger Casaromago" rows were expected to pass on a
      Beauvais-distance, but the site is 314-368 km from Beauvais).

#### stage() staging files are append-only and idempotent on (site, title) - a changed id rule leaves the old rows behind
Where: `stage()` in `fit/src_van_deventer.py` / `fit/src_artists.py` (the per-source staging
      `extras_*.jsonl` / `files_*.jsonl` / `classified_*.jsonl`)
Symptom: after a re-stage where the site-id rule changed (e.g. an inline slug replaced by `catalog.slug`,
      "chi-vres" -> "chievres"), the files hold a row per town under the OLD id plus a second row with the
      same title under the NEW id - the (old_sid, title) pair is already in `have`, so the old row is never
      rewritten or dropped.
Why: stage() appends, and idempotency is per (site, title) pair; a changed id is a new pair. The staging
      files are the task's own and are consolidated by 211 later, so when the id key changes before 211
      runs: delete the three staging files and re-run `stage` (the files then hold one id generation only).

### tools/right_place.py

#### A site is bucketed by web/data/sites.json's "region" - a record without it (or a synthetic tree's) is never flagged, silently
Where: tools/right_place.py (`site_facts`'s `_region_bucket`); any synthetic tree that exercises the
      right-place check (tests/test_fit_queue.py's namesake tree); web/data/sites.json (real records carry
      "England"/"Wales"/"US"/... capitalized)
Symptom: a pairing that is obviously a namesake mismatch (the picture's county word contradicts the site's
      county) is NOT flagged - no error, no warning, the check just finds nothing; it looks like "the check
      is broken" when in fact H1/H2 never fired at all
Why: `site_facts` lowercases the record's `region` and buckets it: england/wales/scotland -> "uk",
      us/usa -> "us", everything else (including missing) -> "other"; H1 only compares across sides of the
      Atlantic, H2 is UK-sites-only, and an "other" bucket matches neither. A sites.json record without
      "region" (or any region string outside the bucketed set) is silently uncheckable. When building a
      synthetic tree for the check, give every record a bucketed region ("England" in the real file's
      capitalization works - the bucket lowercases).

### Wikimedia APIs (Commons, Wikidata)

#### A Commons file page's structured data is a local MediaInfo item (M<page id>), not a global Wikidata item
Where: `fit/evidence.py` (`fetch_page_ids`, `fetch_file_entities`); the Commons API `w/api.php`; any future
      per-file metadata fetching (task 801, and the batch tasks that harvest file pages)
Symptom: searching a file page's HTML for its Wikidata item id (`ItemPage/(Q\d+)`, `"wikibaseItem"`,
      `"globalItem"`) finds nothing (or finds unrelated items: Q13414952 is MD5 - it appears as a P459
      qualifier on the file's content-hash statement; Q19652 is "public domain" - the P6216 license). The
      page's `mw.config` carries `"wbEntityId":"M<page id>"` instead.
Why: files uploaded without a global Wikidata item get a *local* Wikibase entity on Commons (the
      wbmi/"MediaInfo" integration), and its statements are what the file page's "Structured data" tab
      shows. The local wiki's `wbgetentities` answers `ids=M<page id>` directly (the `site` parameter is
      rejected with a warning but not needed; the entity comes back under `"statements"`, not the WD
      service's `"claims"`), and a page that does have a global item answers with `{"missing":"true",
      "normalized":{"item":"Q…"}}` - chase that Q id through the Wikidata service for the real claims.
      Batch 50 ids per call, pace with `commons.get` (1 s).

#### P6216 is the license property, never a depicts claim - do not group it with P180
Where: `fit/evidence.py` (`fetch_file_entities`, `check_depicts`); any regex or dict over wbmi/Wikidata
      statements that treats property lists loosely
Symptom: a statement matcher over the file item that accepts "P180|P6216" as depictions reports
      "public domain" (Q19652) or other license items as depicted entities - a false depiction tie.
Why: MediaInfo items always carry a P6216 (license) statement, so any P180|P6216 alternation is
      guaranteed to pick up licenses. Only P180 (depicts) is a depiction; the site-side depiction
      evidence is P3311 (plan) / P18 (image) on the site's item.

#### The Latin Peutinger names (Casaromago, Sammarobriva) have no Wikidata item; "Peutinger" resolves to a German gymnasium
Where: `fit/evidence.py` (`resolve_places`, the sheet candidate walk, task 801); the Wikidata `wbsearchentities`
Symptom: a search for "Casaromago" or "Sammarobriva" (the Roman names printed on the Dutch Limes sheets) returns
      [] - no place resolution; a search for "Peutinger" returns Q2081791 (Peutinger-Gymnasium Ellwangen,
      10.13E 48.97N) as its first hit, 475-500 km from both Dutch Limes sites.
Why: the Peutinger map's Latin place names were never itemized, and the one surviving "Peutinger" item is the
      gymnasium named after the map's owner. A first-resolved walk over such rows lands on that far item and
      records a conflict (the rows stay `none` with the conflict stored) - never a false pass; if a Latin name
      ever gets an item, the walk picks it up automatically.

#### `commons.members()` returns namespaced titles; subcats need `split(":",1)[1]`, file members must NOT be stripped
Where: `pipeline/commons.py:members`, `fit/src_kip.py:list_files`; any code comparing live category members against
      stored names
Symptom: comparing live subcategory members against bare names ("Britannia Illustrata") fails every comparison -
      the API returns `"Category:Britannia Illustrata"` for subcats but `"File:..."` for files; a drift assert
      comparing the two kinds of titles dies on the first category.
Why: the Commons API `members` call returns the page titles exactly as stored: subcategory pages carry the
      `Category:` prefix, file pages the `File:` prefix. Strip the prefix only for subcats (`split(":",1)[1]`);
      file titles keep `File:` everywhere downstream (inventory keys, staging rows, the `evidence` field) -
      stripping there would desynchronize them from `sources.py` and the canonical rows.

#### The Commons `DateTimeOriginal` (`date` in `commons.info()`) is not always the original's date
Where: `pipeline/commons.py:info()` (the `date` key = extmetadata `DateTimeOriginal`); every consumer that
      records a drawing's age from it (staged file rows, the date column of `docs/lead_kip.md` §3)
Symptom: a scanned print's "date" comes back as a publication sentence ("Published in Reistogt naar en door
      Oostindien, Amsterdam, c. 1775"), an upload date ("5 December 2005 (original upload date)"), or the date
      of a PHOTO of the print (2016-10-26 for a 2016 scan of a 1707 plate) - not the plate's own date.
Why: curators fill DateTimeOriginal inconsistently: for photos it is the shooting date, for book scans often
      the publication's date, sometimes free text. Before using the field to record a plate's age, check what
      the file is (plate scan / photo / book page): the plate's date usually sits in the TITLE or in the
      Rijks-style `Titel(s):` line of the description (the `desc` field), and `stage()` should take it from
      there.

#### From this VM, `iiprop=wbentity` returns nothing for ANY file - the depicts/M-item route is unusable
Where: the Commons API `iiprop=wbentity` (a file -> its MediaInfo item); the planned P180 (depicts) evidence
      route for staged file rows (task 205)
Symptom: the response has no `item` for every file tried: the Gott 112a Temple Newsam scan, the Rijksmuseum
      "Gezicht op Stanway" file, and even "File:Mona Lisa, by Leonardo da Vinci.jpg" (which certainly has a

Why: the mechanism yields nothing from this VM (server-side gating, or the parameter is not served here); it

      staged rows use `caption_coords` (the plate's caption + the verified site point) or the hand-tied QID, and

#### The en.wikipedia API: `action=query` and `action=parse` own disjoint property sets; a missing page is `missing:""` in query, `missingtitle` in parse
Where: `https://en.wikipedia.org/w/api.php` (via `commons.get`, which sets the UA); task 205's infobox checks
      (Kings Weston House, pageid 10102492)
Symptom: `action=parse&prop=coordinates` errors (coordinates is a query prop); `action=query&prop=wikitext`
      errors (wikitext is a parse prop); an absent page under `action=query&titles=` comes back as a page object
      with `"missing":""` - an EMPTY STRING, falsy, so `if page.get("missing")` reads as "present". Under
      `action=parse` the same page gives `"missingtitle":"true"`.
Why: two actions, disjoint prop namespaces; the query missing-marker is the empty string. Test for
      `"missing" in page`. Get the infobox coordinates from `action=query&prop=coordinates` and the article body
      from `action=parse&prop=wikitext` - two calls, never one.
#### wbsearchentities with limit=5 misses well-known short names - Mons (Belgium) ranks 11th in the en search
Where: `fit/src_van_deventer.py` (`_search_candidates`, the default limit 5) and any script calling the
      Wikidata wbsearchentities API for a short, common town name
Symptom: the town's item is simply absent from the five candidates (no error, just a short list) - the
      discovery run records a wrong or no QID; for 'Mons' the five were the planetary nomenclature term 'mons'
      plus French communes (Var, Hérault, Charente, Gard) while the Belgian city Q83407 was 11th (4th in the
      fr search)
Why: short common names get outranked by their many homonyms. When the expected item is not among the five,
      re-search at limit 20 (and in the other language), then re-check label + P625 + P373 + enwiki before
      recording - the 204 BE batch found Mons only this way (lead doc, QID verification - Belgium).

#### A wbsearchentities label search containing parentheses returns EMPTY
Where: the Wikidata wbsearchentities API for a label-based search (fit/src_van_deventer.py
      `_search_candidates`; task 204's 'Luxembourg (city)' lookup)
Symptom: search='Luxembourg (city)' returns [] - no candidates, no error - while the item exists and the
      unparenthesized search 'Luxembourg City' hits it (Q1842 came first at limit 20; the
      plain 'Luxembourg' search ranks the country Q32 and the Belgian province Q1126 ahead of it)
Why: the search matches labels, and '(city)' is a Wikipedia-style disambiguation that no Wikidata label
      carries (the item's label is just 'Luxembourg'). A parenthesized or otherwise qualified search term is a
      guess about a label that does not exist and silently returns nothing. Search the unparenthesized form
      (or a label form that actually exists) and let the candidate fact sheet (label + P625 + P373 + enwiki)
      do the disambiguation.

#### A Wikimedia API call with no User-Agent gets HTTP 403; commons.get already sets one, a raw script must too
Where: `pipeline/commons.py` (`get`, sets `aw.UA`) and any throwaway script hitting the Wikimedia APIs
      directly (e.g. the thumb download snippet of the 204 BE eye check)
Symptom: HTTP Error 403: Forbidden on the very first request; the same request works once a User-Agent is sent
Why: Wikimedia's robot policy rejects requests without a descriptive User-Agent. `aw.UA` is the project's
      standard value: a DICT ({"User-Agent": ...}), not a string - pass it to urllib's Request(headers=)
      as-is, but slicing it like a string (UA[:60]) raises KeyError. A raw urllib script must set it (or go
      through `commons.get`, which paces and retries too).

#### upload.wikimedia.org rate-limits raw FILE downloads separately from the API: 3 back-to-back full-file fetches 429'd on the 4th
Where: any bulk download of Commons file bytes (209b's category-scan visual check, /tmp/agent-a-209b/dl2.py; any fit/src_*.py that fetches originals)
Symptom: urllib HTTPError 429 "Too many requests (f061ab2)" on the 4th consecutive full-file download from upload.wikimedia.org, while the w/api.php metadata calls (paced via commons.get) never 429'd at all
Why: the CDN that serves the file bytes owns a separate, stricter limit than the API endpoints - pacing the API does not pace the downloads. Space file downloads ~30+ s apart with backoff on a 429 (retry after 60 s); the metadata API is the cheap path, the file bytes the expensive one.

#### de.wikipedia `list=allimages` paginates via the `aicontinue` continue key - `aifrom`/`aipfrom` do not advance
Where: de.wikipedia `w/api.php?action=query&list=allimages` (task 208's 874-file ORL set; any large prefix listing on de.wiki)
Symptom: re-issuing the call with `aifrom` (or `aipfrom`) set to the last image name returns the SAME first page forever - the loop never advances past the first N images
Why: for allimages the API's `continue` object carries only `aicontinue`; the from-parameters of other list endpoints are not honoured here. Pass the response's `continue` object back verbatim.

#### Never read a plate legend or scale off a low-dpi render - both 1895 ORL Tafel scales were misread that way
Where: low-resolution page renders/thumbnails of large-format plates (task 208's ORL 1895 volume; any small preview of a plate with dense legends)
Symptom: the Situationskarte's MAASSTAB 1:5000 looked like "1:3000" and the fort plan's 1:1000 like "~1:500" at 40 dpi - both wrong, found only at 70 dpi+ re-renders
Why: in small renders the digits of dense plate legends blur into each other (5~3, 1~0). Read legends, scales and signatures only from full-resolution page images (e.g. an IA `page/n{N}.jpg`); if still ambiguous, crop the legend and upscale before recording a value.

#### de.wikipedia `titles=File:X` normalizes to `Datei:<name with SPACES>` - look results up by the normalized name
Where: de.wikipedia `action=query&titles=...&prop=imageinfo` lookups (task 208's de.wiki file metadata)
Symptom: `pages["File:ORL_40_tab_04_pic_01_Grundriss.jpg"]` KeyErrors - the returned key is `Datei:ORL 40 tab 04 pic 01 Grundriss.jpg` (German ns prefix, underscores turned into spaces)
Why: MediaWiki canonicalizes titles: the namespace prefix is localized (`File:` -> `Datei:` on de.wiki) and underscores become spaces. Build the lookup key by stripping the ns prefix, lowercasing and unifying space/underscore on both sides.

#### `wbsearchentities` returns `description` (and `label`) as a bare STRING when called with `language=de`
Where: Wikidata `wbsearchentities` with an explicit language (task 208's QID phase - crashed leg_b_meta after ~11 of ~28 searches)
Symptom: `hit["description"]["value"]` raises `TypeError: string indices must be integers` - the field is a plain string, not a dict
Why: without `language` the service returns multilingual dicts; with it, plain strings. Handle both: `v = d.get("value") if isinstance(d, dict) else d`.

#### Zero-padded fort-number searches ("Kastell 01 Limes") find no Wikidata item - search the label, not the number
Where: Wikidata `wbsearchentities` for the ORL forts (task 208's leg_c: ten forts were lost to this in the first pass)
Symptom: `search="Kastell 01 Limes"` (and `Kastell 1 Limes`, `Kastell 05a Limes`) return [] although the item exists ("Kastell Heddesdorf")
Why: item labels never contain the ORL number, and a zero-padded number plus a "Limes" suffix forms a query that matches nothing. Search by name with variants ("Kastell X", "X (Kastell)", "X (Limes)", "Römerkastell X", "Kastelle von X"); the number is only a routing key in your own table.

#### The `action=wbgetentities` response key is `entities`, not `pages` - `d.get("pages")` silently returns {}
Where: Wikidata `wbgetentities` (task 208's leg_d: step 3 silently dropped all three new QID entities)
Symptom: no error at all - `d.get("pages", {})` is always {}, so downstream code continues with an empty entity set
Why: `wbgetentities` returns `{qid: entity}` under `"entities"`; `"pages"` is the MediaWiki `action=query` shape. Use `d.get("entities", {})` and check `d.get("missing")`.

#### Wikidata search is spelling-exact for umlauts: "Oehringen" finds nothing, "Öhringen" finds the items
Where: Wikidata `wbsearchentities` (task 208's fort 42: Q86069877/Q91949042 were found only via the Ö-spelling)
Symptom: every ASCII-transliterated phrasing ("Oehringen", "Oehringen (Kastell)", "Kastell Oehringen") returns []; the identical query with the native spelling returns the items immediately
Why: the search matches against the labels as stored (native script); transliterations are different strings. Try the native (German) spelling first, ASCII variants only as fallback.

#### de.wikipedia `srsearch "<name> Limes"` can miss a fort article - try direct titles (`Kastell X`, `X (Kastell)`, `Kastelle von X`) first
Where: de.wikipedia `action=query&list=search` (srsearch) and `action=query&titles=...&prop=pageprops` (task 208's final no-QID check, forts 64/67)
Symptom: `srsearch 'Kastell Schirenhof Limes'` returns [] although the article "Kastell Schirenhof" exists (and "Kastelle von Neckarburken" exists as a PLURAL title covering two forts)
Why: small-fort article titles on de.wiki vary ("Kastell X", "X (Kastell)", "Kastelle von X") and the "Limes" suffix is often absent, so a phrase query with extra tokens drops them below the search limit. For a known fort, query the direct title candidates with `pageprops=wikibase_item` (it returns the QID when the article carries one) and use srsearch only as a last resort.

#### Wikidata through this machine's proxy intermittently returns 200 responses with a GZIP body urllib does not decode
Where: the Wikidata API (`wbgetentities`, `wbsearchentities`) as called via this VM's HTTP proxy (`pipeline/commons.py:get`, `pipeline/catalog_wd.py`; 236a, 2026-10-13)
Symptom: a few % of otherwise-valid calls (worse while several agents share the IP and hit Wikimedia at once) return HTTP 200 whose body is gzip-compressed; `json.loads` gets the raw bytes and dies with `json.JSONDecodeError: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)`. A naive retry loop fails 3-4 times in a row before one call comes through plain; the same query a moment later succeeds. The Commons API (commons.wikimedia.org) was reliable all session.
Why: the proxy occasionally hands back a gzip-encoded body that urllib does not auto-decode. Fix: send the request header `Accept-Encoding: identity`, or use `pipeline/catalog_wd.py` (disk cache + 20 retries + 429 backoff - it got through with visible "wd 429, waiting 47s" retries); that layer is the right tool for bulk Wikidata work from this machine.

#### Commons file titles are case-sensitive: a title remembered with the wrong case returns empty imageinfo and looks deleted
Where: the Commons `action=query&titles=...&prop=imageinfo` (`pipeline/commons.py:info`); 236a's Ratzer 1776 files, 2026-10-13
Symptom: the batch query for `File:Plan of the City of New York by Ratzer, 1776.jpg` (capital-C "City") came back with no url - it looked deleted (stale search index), while the search list showed the real page `File:Plan of the city of New York by Ratzer, 1776.jpg` (lowercase "city") next door: live, PD, 2202x1446.
Why: MediaWiki page titles are case-sensitive except in the first character; a mid-title "city"/"City" is a different page. When an expected file looks missing, search first (`srnamespace 6`) and use the exact title from the results, never the remembered one.

#### The Wikimedia thumb API accepts only certain widths: 1280 and 1920 work, 2400/2560 come back 400
Where: `thumb.wikimedia.org` thumb URLs (`.../wikipedia/commons/thumb/<x>/<xx>/<File>/NNNpx-<File>`), the research thumb-eyeballing workflow (241, 2026-10-14)
Symptom: requesting `/2400px-...` (or `/2560px-...`) of an 11764-px original returns HTTP 400 "Use thumbnail sizes listed on https://w.wiki/GHai", while `/1280px-...` and `/1920px-...` succeed
Why: the thumb endpoint serves only a fixed set of widths (listed at w.wiki/GHai); 1920 is the largest confirmed working (a ~5 MB JPEG for an 11764-px original). For zooms request the 1920-px thumb and use the PIL resize-then-crop path (a direct PIL crop save can render blank in the read tool).

#### Commons search matches file titles case-insensitively but OCR full text case-sensitively: a city whose mirror pool is empty returns 0 for every form, and only lowercase variants surface OCR-text hits
Where: the Commons search API (`action=query&list=search&srnamespace=6`, `pipeline/commons.py:get`), the 236b/241 pool builders, 2026-10-14 (task 241's Albuquerque probe)
Symptom: all six documented pool forms for Albuquerque ("bird's-eye view of Albuquerque", "Albuquerque bird's eye", ...) returned 0, while the lowercase "albuquerque bird's eye" returned 5 hits and "albuquerque aerial view" matched TITLES whose name is capitalized ("File:Albuquerque - aerial view of ...jpg") - so the query's casing decides which fields can hit, and a city with no file-title match looks exactly like "no such files".
Why: the title field matches case-insensitively either way, but the OCR full-text field matches case-sensitively (book body text is indexed lowercase; a capitalized query word never matches it). When a city's pool comes back 0/0/0/0/0/0 that is a signal, not a rate-limit: before dropping the city, probe (a) the six forms with the city name in LOWERCASE, (b) the LOC Panoramic title variants that do not say "bird's eye" ("Panoram of <name>", "<name> LOC", "<name> LCCN"), and (c) "<state> bird eye view" (that last one surfaced the drawn Santa Fe / Las Vegas, N.M. 1882 sheets that city-level queries missed). Record every probe in the lead doc.

### fit/

#### record._fake_match takes the fixture's responses dict, not the fixture
Where: `tests/fixtures/matchfit_station/record.py` (`_fake_match`); offline replays of the 302f/
      238 fixtures (`records.json`, `records_unsure.json`)
Symptom: passing the whole fixture to `rec._fake_match(fixture)` KeyErrors on every /match
      request (the lookup is by sha256 of the exact request body, which never matches a fixture
      top-level key) - matchfit prints `matcher error on <ground> x<f>: '<sha256>'` for every
      window and fit_row reports "the matcher found nothing consistent".
Why: `_fake_match(records)` does `records[hashlib.sha256(body).hexdigest()]`; the fixture's top
      level is `{header, responses}`, so pass `fixture["responses"]` (the flat sha256 -> response
      map). test_matchfit_station.py's in-process stub never hits this: it hashes the live request
      body against the same dict itself.

#### Python binds `/` and `%` at the same precedence (left-associative), and `or` binds below both
Where: `fit/batch_us.py` (`write_report`, path building), `tests/test_batch_us.py`
      (`_check_doc`, `_check_doc_stub`)
Symptom: `Path(root) / "a" / "%s.json" % (x, y)` raises `TypeError: unsupported operand type(s)
      for %: 'PosixPath' and 'tuple'` - the expression parses as `(Path(root) / "a" / "%s.json") %
      (x, y)`. Likewise `"a" or "b" / "c"` parses as `"a" or ("b" / "c")` (one silent wrong-value
      hit and one crash in the batch work).
Why: in Python's precedence table `* / // %` form one level, `+ -` the next, then comparisons,
      then `not` / `and` / `or`. So a `%` formatting applied to a path string is swallowed into the
      `/` chain before it, and a `/` into an `or`. Always parenthesize a format string inside a
      chain: `Path(root) / ("a%s.json" % (x, y))`; never mix `/` with `or` unparenthesized.

#### `batch_us.pre_docs` matches any existing `<site>.*.json` document - including automatic docs the current run just wrote
Where: `fit/batch_us.py` (`pre_docs`, `run_sites`), `tests/test_batch_us.py`
Symptom: code that computes a site's "pre-batch" state AFTER `run_sites` treats every candidate as
      already pre-fit: for serpent-mound the expected set comes out empty and an assertion compares
      15 new automatic documents against `set()` - which looks like a gate-verdict mismatch, but
      the gate (pipeline/fit_gate.py) is a pure function of (pairs, transform) plus frozen module
      constants, so two identical calls cannot disagree.
Why: `pre_docs` scans data/db/platefits/ as it stands at call time, and the batch writes its
      automatic documents into that same directory during the run. Snapshot the pre-run state
      (`pre_docs`, `is_pre_fit`) BEFORE calling `run_sites`; compare the post-run directory only for
      "what is new". (Session-3 misdiagnosis: it first read as cross-test state pollution.)

#### Recorded-answer batch tests must be state-aware: an earlier run's auto docs are pre-docs for the next run's recorded model
Where: `tests/test_batch_eu.py` (`test_hand_fitted_sites_get_items_for_their_other_pictures`),
      `fit/batch_us.py` (`run_sites`'s skip rule), `fit/batch_eu.py`
Symptom: a test that pins an item's expected candidates against the full candidate list passes on
      the pre-run tree and fails after the working run ("Extra items in the right set: c_..."): the
      plans the run turned into automatic documents are skipped as pre-docs by the test's recorded
      run (never re-fitted, no entry) and never appear in the item.
Why: `run_sites` skips any candidate whose doc exists at call time (`have = pre_docs ∪ docs written
      this run`), and the test's temp tree copy carries the previous run's documents. Expectations
      computed from a static list of candidate ids go stale the moment any run adds a document -
      this also hits 212's re-coverage run, which adds docs for grown sites.
Do this instead: compute expectations from the live tree state at test time: fresh = candidates
      minus `pre_docs` (re-read in the test, never a constant), expected item candidates = the live
      item's candidates (a working run may have left one) ∪ fresh (exact equality), and assert the
      post-run invariants (one file per site, named after candidates[0].plan; resolved unchanged).
      The test then passes before and after every run.

Where: `tools/gate_heldout.py` (`partition`), `tests/test_gate.py` (`test_recorded_measurement_reproduces_and_agrees`), `data/db/platefits/`
Symptom: `gate_heldout: expected 20 hand-fit documents in data/db/platefits/, found 21; the registered partition is void, see docs/gate.md section 1`; `tests/test_gate.py` is the suite's one red test on main as of 2026-10-11 (the driver's `.agent/reports/last-failing-tests.txt` records it; my 302a run reproduced it byte-identically, 59 passed / 1 failed).
Why: the one-shot registration (docs/gate.md section 3, seed 20260108) is frozen over exactly the 20 named pre-registration hand fits; `partition()` re-derives the name list from ALL non-auto documents and demands exactly 20, so every new hand fit (the lead's 21st: cd104ca maiden-castle c_c20ff6b1f16d173d; 206's shotwick-castle c_e6e5490609414bb9; the 207 Roman fits) aborts the command.
Do this instead: do not edit `tools/gate_heldout.py` or `tests/test_gate.py` from any other task, and do not "fix" the failure by touching the registration or the documents. The fix is tasks/218 (agent a, open, `Depends on: 001`): tolerate additional post-registration hand docs while requiring the 20 named ones to stay present and unchanged. If your task needs the suite green, note the failure as pre-existing in your hand-over and move on; the driver's baseline re-check accepts it for other tasks' done claims.

#### `data/db/platefits/` mixes hand fits and automatic ones (`"auto": true`) - code that counts the directory's files must filter `doc.get("auto")`
Where: `tools/gate_heldout.py` (`partition`), `fit/batch_us.py` (`write_doc`, `write_golden`), `data/db/platefits/`
Symptom: code that treats every `data/db/platefits/*.json` as a hand-fit reference breaks once a batch

      pre-802 `gate_heldout partition()` aborted with "expected 20 hand-fit documents in

Why: the batch writes its accepted fits into that same directory (`write_doc`), but the
      golden/held-out reference is the 20 hand fits, which 203a's golden pins byte-identical after
      the run. Count or list the NON-automatic set: `if not json.load(open(p)).get("auto")`
      (the `write_golden` criterion; a doc without the field is a hand fit). Automatic documents
      only ever ADD names - a hand-fit doc never gains the field - so any derivation over the

#### The one-shot gate registration is frozen at the 20 NAMED hand-fit docs, not "whatever is in the directory" - post-218 partition() derives over exactly those names and excludes all post-registration docs; a registered name that stops being non-automatic genuinely voids the registration (before 218 merged, a 21st hand doc instead tripped the "expected 20" precondition)
Where: `tools/gate_heldout.py` (`partition`, `REGISTERED`), `data/db/platefits/`, `tests/test_gate.py`, docs/gate.md sections 1 and 3
