#### This Qwen fabricates correspondences that pass a consistency-only gate; the batch's prompt/parse/scale/texture checks are the counterweight
Where: `fit/batch_us.py` (`llm_model`, `_model_prompt`, `_parse_answer`, `_feature_present`), the local qwen3.8-27b via
      `pipeline/llm.py`, docs/gate.md section 7
Symptom: asked to match features between two gridded panels, the model answers with internally
      perfect but false correspondences (identity (100,100)->(100,100)..., the four corners to the
      four corners, a 5-point diagonal ladder, a 1:1 pixel line ~281 m off the 202 seed): gate med
      ~0.0 m, and the frozen gate ACCEPTS them - docs/gate.md section 7: a consistency check cannot
      see a consistent global error. Unopposed, every automatic batch document would be garbage and
      the human's 18/20 report-sample check would fail.
Why: a 27 B vision model that cannot confidently read a figure (e.g. a small figure on a dense
      text page) invents a regular grid-like correspondence instead of reporting few pairs. The
      gate is frozen, so the counterweight is batch-side: a prompt giving both panels' labelled
      coordinate ranges + metre coverage, a +/-50% seed-scale window, anti-pattern clauses (no
      grid-line intersections / even spacing / >=3 collinear; never pad a list) and asking for
      named features plus a stated scale; parsing drops pairs outside the labelled ranges; a
      stated scale that disagrees >=2x with the MAGNITUDE of the model's own points' similarity
      trims the answer to 3 pairs (a review item, never an automatic document); and a
      feature-presence check (`_feature_present`) trims an answer whose ground points mostly sit
      on less textured ground than the median of a 400-point null of the site's own image. The
      last one is needed for a fifth class the other checks all pass (4c pilot, tremper): a
      correct-scale, wrong-translation answer whose points sit on structureless ground. The
      checks only ever route to review; a fabrication anchored on strong texture (roads, field
      boundaries) passes all of them - docs/gate.md section 7's human 18/20 sample is the
      backstop for that class.

#### 201's upsert merges item candidates by whole-entry replacement per plan - a subset-shaped entry drops the denormalized row fields; the page's row lookup, not the entry, covers the save flow
Where: `fit/review.py` (`upsert_item`), `fit/batch_us.py` (`write_item`), `data/review/*.json`,
      `web/review.js` (`rvResolveRow`), `web/index.html` (`openPlan`), `tests/test_review.py`
      (`test_save_resolves_the_item`)
Symptom: after a consumer upserts a candidate whose entry lacks the page-save fields, code that
      reads them from the ITEM ENTRY fails with KeyError: the 203a batch's entry shape (plan,
      title, url, evidence, pairs, coarse, ground, scale_m_px, rot_deg, scale_source, note,
      why, gate_score) replaced the 201-seed entry for alligator's n0214_2 (which also stored
      map_box, size, ia, file, label, book, cite, view), and the test died with
      `KeyError: 'map_box'`. The page itself never misbehaved.
Why: `upsert_item`'s documented merge is "a same-plan entry replaces the existing one in
      place" - fields absent from the incoming entry are simply gone. But the page does not
      rely on the stored copies: `rvResolveRow` resolves the candidate's row from
      web/data/plans.json by (plan, site) FIRST, and the stored-field fallback (missing
      map_box tolerated, `openPlan` falls back to the full frame) exists only for rows absent
      from the current build. Read those fields from the plans.json ROW (map_box, size, ia,
      file, label, book, cite, view are all row columns) - never from an item's entry, which
      any later upsert may have re-shaped.

#### A binary rasterisation of a small disc (7-12 px) carries a 0.3-0.8 px systematic centroid bias that no supersample fixes
Where: `tests/test_surveyfit.py` (`_rasterize`, `_centroids`, `match_response`); applies to any synthetic ink world
Symptom: the connected-component centroid of a disc drawn at a known (sub-)pixel centre sits 0.3-0.8 px from the true centre; 8x supersampling is WORSE than 4x (0.33 -> 0.71 px for r = 3.5), doubling the radius barely helps (0.48-0.88 px); a JPEG q95 roundtrip and a 42 deg PIL bicubic rotation add at most ~0.05 px on top
Why: thresholding per-pixel coverage at 0.3 cuts the disc edge asymmetrically about the sub-pixel centre; for a small blob the edge-pixel ring dominates the centroid, and finer supersampling only changes which edge pixels land inside, not the asymmetry. Consequence: in the stub matcher the ink centroids are good for glyph DETECTION only (within 2 px of the expected spot); a returned keypoint is modelled as a sub-pixel regression (the expected rotated position + a deterministic +-0.25 px wobble + the 0.6 px/deg quality jitter). Never expect a blob centroid to be sub-pixel ground truth in a synthetic world.

#### A fit/src_*.py CLI that lazily imports pipeline modules needs its own sys.path insert at module top - tests hide it
Where: fit/src_wiltshire_hoare.py (status()/register() import books lazily; src_mackenzie.py does the insert at top); every new fit/src_*.py CLI
Symptom: `python fit/src_wiltshire_hoare.py --status` -> ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'books' while the pytest suite passes
Why: the test file inserts pipeline/ (and fit/) into sys.path before importing the module, but bare `python <script>` puts only the script's own directory on the path. Do `sys.path.insert(0, <root>/pipeline)` at module top (the src_mackenzie.py idiom) so the CLI and the tests share one import path.

#### A `view: true` plans row fits with the 8-parameter homFit, whose result has NO mpx/rot keys - and a 0.0 residual on 4 (or near-collinear) points proves nothing about placement
Where: fit/fitkit (refit/simFit/homFit), web/review.js (openPlan on a view row), audit [eval] lines (tools/audit_306b.mjs / audit_306c.mjs)
Symptom: `[eval]` reports `mpx:null, rot:null` for a view-row fit (not an error); 306c's two view docs (the Baer 1889 serpent: resid 22/61/27/0; the Harper's 1902 serpent: resid 0.0) both sit 180-200 m off the real effigy despite the small residuals
Why: refit() takes the 8-parameter homFit path for `view: true` rows (no scale/rotation constraint), so the result carries no mpx/rot; a homography through 4 points is exact BY CONSTRUCTION, and 8 near-collinear points are under-constrained perpendicular to the anchor line (there the normal-equations solve reports a non-zero resid that measures conditioning, not placement). Judge placement of a view row from the rendered shot against the ground, never from the residual.

#### data/review/*.json items are single indent=1 JSON objects, not JSONL - a line-by-line scanner drowns in fragments

#### Staging -> canonical path mapping must be a stem map, never string surgery: source names contain underscores
Where: staging naming `data/{catalog,commons}/<stem>_<source>.jsonl`; `tests/test_merge.py` (`_canon_of`), `fit/merge.py` (`source_of`)

Why: a staging filename is `<stem>_<source>.jsonl` and the source name itself may carry underscores (wiltshire_b, van_deventer). #### After 211's live merge, every source module's "no staged row in canonical" guard self-triggers - identical twins are the merged state, not a clash
Where: every fit/src_<lead>.py guard that reads the canonical data/commons/files.jsonl or data/catalog/extras.jsonl (van_deventer, kip, mackenzie, limes, numancia, wiltshire_stukeley, artists - tasks 204/205/206/208/210/209b/213), and their test files
Symptom: after running fit/merge.py merge on the real tree, the module's --check (or stage command) reds with "staged title already in the canonical files.jsonl: ..." / SystemExit, and the known-site checks ("staged site re-uses existing QID", "staged site ids collide") false-positive on the module's OWN merged sites
Why: merge.py's contract is that the staging files stay in place and each source's --check still reads them, so "staged row present in the canonical file" is the NORMAL post-merge state, not a clash. A clash is only a DIFFERENT row holding the same key (or an id/QID held by a different site). known_sites() reads the canonical extras, which after the merge contain the source's own staged sites - that is a self-reference, not a duplicate.
What to do: accept a row identical to its canonical twin under the merge's norm() (json.dumps sort_keys, ensure_ascii=False) as an already-merged no-op (check rc 0, stage a no-op); keep fail-loud for a different row with the same key; exclude self-references from known-site collisions (id: staged_ids & (known.values() - staged_ids); QID: known[qid] != staged id). The guard extensions were filed as tasks 222-228 (one module each; 211 depends on them). 222 (fit/src_van_deventer.py + its three-state test) is the reference implementation of the pattern; 223-228 copy it (notes: stukeley's stage leg is also red; mackenzie's guard is named check and its stage leg is the site-id guard on the canonical extras.jsonl - its three-state test covers a fresh re-stage onto a merged tree with the staging files emptied; numancia has no staged site, so its three-state test varies only the canonical files.jsonl, leaving the catalog extras and sites.json reads as-is; artists 228 deviates on the id check: per-site - a staged id is a problem when a known site holding it has a different QID - because the set-difference form above cannot report "a staged id held by a different site" (the id is in staged_ids, so the subtraction removes it); 228's three-state test pins it in (c3)). Fixed: 222-228 (all seven done, iteration 198, 2026-10-12).

#### The roman books' (e) identity check fires on the volatile checked date: stage() stamps location_check.checked = now() but _canon_norm is a full-row dump - a daily red on main (the maclauchlan half is FIXED by 817 it.239; the horsley half is open in 818)
Where: fit/src_roman_maclauchlan.py and fit/src_roman_horsley.py (`_canon_norm` - a copy of fit/merge.py's `norm` - and the (e) check in check_staged/join_problems; `stage()` stamps `now()` into location_check.checked and the file rows' evidence.checked); tests/test_src_roman_maclauchlan.py::test_check_staged_joins_and_passes; the fix is tasks 817 (the 207b module - done 2026-10-15, iteration 239: _canon_norm zeroes the date, stage() restored to the live now() stamp, 230's interim CHECKED constant removed) and 818 (the 809 module - open)
Symptom: `join: staged site luguvallium-q71551754 differs from its canonical row in extras.jsonl` - the maclauchlan test red'd main daily from 2026-10-15 (and 814's done-claim was rejected on exactly this red, 816's Why section) even though the staged row is otherwise identical to its canonical twin - FIXED by 817 it.239 (the zeroing makes it green on any day; the test's (d)/(e) controls pin both directions of the skew); the same latent is still in the horsley check (green today only because it reads the committed rows, not a fresh stage())
Why: stage() stamps the staging date (now()) into location_check.checked, the canonical row carries the 211/230 re-run's re-stamp date (2026-10-14 on main), and _canon_norm compares the whole row including that date - so (e) "identical to the canonical row" fails on the date field alone (809 measured it at 199: all 9 staged roman site rows dict-identical to canonical; a fresh stage() differs ONLY on location_check.checked). It is daily and self-healing (green on the re-stamp day, red the next; the 197 "resolved" state lasted exactly one day) - the module's own golden _norm already zeros both checked dates for exactly this reason ("they vary with the staging").

#### fit/cover.py `_fetch_one` took a PosixPath and did `dst + ".part"` - the per-file except swallowed the TypeError as if it were a network failure
Where: fit/cover.py `_fetch_one` (fixed 2026-10-13, 212a: `dst = str(dst)`), `_fetch_local` (passes the Path), tests/test_cover.py (its tree hard-links every local copy, so `p.exists()` short-circuits and the download path is NEVER exercised by the tests)
Symptom: every real download fails with "fetch failed <url>: unsupported operand type(s) for +: 'PosixPath' and 'str'" (printed, rc False, retried on the next run - it looks like a flaky network, but it was a type bug on every attempt); the files never appear, stage records "no local copy (fetch failed, retried next run)" for each.
Why: `_fetch_one`'s broad `except Exception` was written for network failures and reports any exception as a fetch failure; a type error in its own `open(dst + ".part")` line then masqueraded as a per-file download failure, and the tests can't see it because their trees already contain the copies (the live 212a run was the first to actually download).
What to do: when a "network" failure is uniform (every file fails, identical message), suspect the code path itself - reproduce with one direct call outside the try/except.

#### tools/export_plans.py's commons rows are the CLASSIFIER's output: only plan/birdseye pictures become plans.json rows, so a staged picture need not grow the file
Where: tools/export_plans.py `commons_rows` (a files.jsonl row gets a plans row only when classified.jsonl has it with `p_photo < 0.5` AND `max(p_plan, p_birdseye) >= 0.3` (min_p) and a local copy exists), fit/cover.py stage (re-exports after staging), web/data/plans.json
Symptom: after staging N new pictures, plans.json grows by far fewer than N rows (212a live run: 107 staged -> 35 rows on 11 of the 16 sites; the other 5 sites' pictures were all photos/views/engravings below the gate). This is the DESIGN, not a failure: plans.json is the plate-fit input, so only plan/birdseye candidates go in; the photos stay in files.jsonl (with their classified + evidence fields) and the no-picture/loop phases work from the sites, not from plans.json growth.
What to do: don't "fix" a short growth by lowering min_p or adding rows by hand; the (id, sites[0]) key-set diff (pure adds, 0 lost) is the check, and a site whose pictures all fall below the gate is legitimately still a no-picture site.

#### np.abs on an (n,2) point array is per-element, not the per-row radius; broadcasting (n,1) against it silently yields (n,n,2)
Where: any numpy work over `[x, y]` point arrays in ground metres (238's gate measurements: `pipeline/fit_gate.py` `score` shapes; throwaway /tmp scripts that distort a doc's pairs before re-gating)
Symptom: per-row scale factors computed as `rho[:, None] / rho.max()` style or `np.abs(z - C)` on a complex-free (n,2) array give per-element magnitudes, and any `(n,1) * (n,2)` product you build from them silently broadcasts to (n,n,2) - the gate then runs on garbage pairs without any error (med/slope look plausible).
Why: numpy's abs is elementwise; the row-wise magnitude of (x, y) is the COMPLEX magnitude `abs(x + 1j*y)`, which is what `fit_gate.score`/`matchfit.ransac` do internally. Do the distortion/scale math in complex form (`z = x + 1j*y`), never in (n,1)x(n,2) outer-product form.

#### The bird's-eye pool's "the caption names the city" gate is a substring match - incidental mentions pass, so every gate-pass item must be eyeballed
Where: the LOC Panoramic Maps pool scripts and `fit/src_us_birdseye*.py` (`evidence_for`, the pool gate `books_match.norm(name) in books_match.norm(title + " " + desc)`); observed on the Omaha pool at 241 iter-175 (/tmp/aw241_omaha_pool.json)
Symptom: the pool's "good" list contains items that are not views of the city at all: stereoscopic photo cards from a series whose line says "Across the continent west from Omaha", a postcard whose back text mentions the city (a Minneapolis sheet), a regional railroad-promo sheet whose copyright line says "...Omaha, Nebr.", a sheet captioned "846 miles west of Omaha" (Green River, WY), a book index page listing a bird's-eye of a different city.
Why: `books_match.norm()` lowercases and strips punctuation, and the gate is a bare `in` (substring) over title + description, so any incidental mention in those fields passes. In the pool the gate is a coarse pre-filter, not a selector: eyeball every gate-pass item's 1280 px thumb before picking (the 236b/240/241 practice). In the staging modules the same substring test is the last line (stage fails loud when the caption does not print the city) - there it is sound because the title is already hand-chosen, which is why a false-positive pool item never reaches a staged row.

      added 2026-10-11 by task 300 after its bare-urllib `load_picture` was the one unpaced live fetcher);

      fit/src_van_deventer.py --list/--verify/--files/--chain)
Symptom: HTTP 429 from commons.wikimedia.org or wikidata.org `w/api.php` after a dozen or so consecutive
      calls, even when paced 1-2 s apart
Why: Wikimedia rate-limits per-client bursts well below 1 req/s in practice. `commons.get()` is
      Retry-After-aware (it sleeps the server's value and retries) - use it (or replicate its pacing) instead
      of a bare urllib call with a fixed sleep; a 26-call verify run completed in ~30 s wall on 2026-10-11
      with no manual intervention. Never loop a hand-rolled fetcher without the Retry-After handling.

#### A platefit doc's `size` is the browser image's size, not the big cache file's - `m_per_px` in depictions.json depends on the big image's dimensions
Where: `pipeline/plan_fit.py` (`load_picture`, `similarity`, `build`); `data/db/platefits/*.json`
      (`size`, `crop`, `pairs`); `web/data/sites/*/depictions.json` (`fit.m_per_px`)
Symptom: re-running plan_fit.build on a stand-in picture sized like `doc["size"]` writes a depictions entry
      whose `m_per_px` differs from the stored one (for stonehenge's 7 docs, 3 of the big cache files are
      1.19-1.75x the doc size: c_098c4cb138676939's stored m_per_px 0.6686 becomes 0.5622 at fs=1), while
      every other field (corners, resid_m, rot_deg, source line) is unchanged.
Why: the page's plate tool places `pairs`/`crop` in the displayed image's pixels (`doc["size"]`), and the
      overlay is built from a bigger rendering of the same file: `load_picture` returns `fs =
      big.width/size[0]`, and solving the similarity on the scaled pairs divides m_per_px by fs. The pixels
      never enter the fit at all (pure least squares over the point pairs), so a stand-in image at the
      EXACT big-image dimensions (read from the cache file's PIL header) reproduces depictions.json
      byte-for-byte with any pixel content (flat colour is fine); one sized like `doc["size"]` (fs=1) does
      not. That is how tests/test_site_done.py stays network-free and byte-exact (task 300).

#### `plan_fit.main()` with no root (and the CLI, which has no --root flag) sweeps the real checkout's whole store - never call it bare in verification
Where: `pipeline/plan_fit.py` (`main`, `build`, `load_picture`, the `if __name__` block); any interactive
      or test session that wants to exercise the sync loop
Symptom: a verification that calls `plan_fit.main([])` (or `plan_fit.py [args]`) without a `root=`/temp
      tree rebuilds EVERY not-current document in the checkout's data/db/platefits (as of 2026-10-11 that
      was ~76 docs), downloads each commons picture's big jpg from Wikimedia at 1/s pacing (tens of
      minutes), and calls `build_site.set_drawings` per site - i.e. it mutates web/data/sites.json -
      until a hard timeout kills it mid-sweep (burned an iteration-94 session; the rebuilt webps turned
      out byte-identical and the only diff was the sites.json drawing refresh).
Why: `main` defaults `_root(None)` to this checkout's ROOT, and the CLI passes `sys.argv[1:]` straight
      in as doc ids (an arg like `--root` is parsed as a doc id). For hermetic verification call
      `plan_fit.main(args, root=<temp tree>)` in-process and seed the tree's
      `web/data/sites/<sid>/depictions.json` with matching `fit.at`/`fit.doc` entries where you want
      `is_done` to skip the build (an unseeded doc's build reaches `load_picture`: book docs fail fast
      with FileNotFoundError, commons docs hit the network).

#### The serve worker's plan_fit sweep aborts on any non-SystemExit mid-sweep - one bad doc strands the rest of that wake
Where: `server/serve.py` (`after_write`'s worker thread: `except BaseException: print(...)` around
      `plan_fit.main([])`); `pipeline/plan_fit.py` (`main`'s per-doc `except SystemExit` only)
Symptom: after a page save, only the documents earlier in alphabetical order get synced; the worker
      prints `plan_fit failed: KeyError('imageinfo')` (a bad commons `ref`) or a 429/urllib error, and
      the remaining docs of that wake are simply never built - they stay not-current until the next
      save. As of 2026-10-11, 76 of the checkout's 116 platefit docs are in that not-current state
      (nearly all commons-sourced, only one with its big jpg cached).
Why: `main` catches `SystemExit` per doc (site not built, bad pairs, task-303 provenance refusal all
      stop only that doc) but any other exception (FileNotFoundError on a missing book scan,
      `KeyError` from an API answer without `imageinfo`, a timeout) escapes `main` into the worker's
      catch-all, which logs it and waits for the NEXT wake - the rest of this wake is lost. A test or
      run that wakes the worker against a tree with a bad doc must expect a partial sweep; making the
      sweep per-doc-proof is not task 303's job.

Where: `tools/site_done.py` (main: fit -> sync -> entry -> review) run without `--root` in this checkout

Why: the line is scoped to one site by design (docs/site_flow.md, "Files the line touches"), and the

#### Verifying a year-once source line by substring: the label string can occur inside the title itself
Where: `pipeline/plan_fit.py` (`source_line`'s commons branch); any verification of built
      depictions (docs whose title carries the label: avaricum's "(1898) (14594767238)",
      bolsover/castle-rising/shotwick's "The Castles of England (1897)")
Symptom: a check like `"(label)" in source` flags CORRECT fixed lines, because the label string
      (e.g. "1897") occurs inside the title's own parenthesis, not as an appended one
Why: source_line appends the label parenthesis after the title, but the title itself may contain
      the same string (Mackenzie plate titles end in the book's year; avaricum's raw file name
      ends in a 10-digit id). The structural test that matches the rule exactly is
      `source.split(", Wikimedia Commons:")[0] == title` (nothing appended after the title for a
      yeared title), which the 219 re-bake verification uses.

#### The dep entry's FILE name strips the site prefix, but its fit.doc keeps the full doc id - audit overlays with the is_done triple or you get false missing/stale
Where: `web/data/sites/<sid>/depictions.json` (the entries plan_fit.build writes, keyed by `file`);
      `pipeline/plan_fit.py` (`build`, `is_done`); any audit that joins `data/db/platefits/*.json`
      docs to their overlays
Symptom: joining docs to overlay entries by the doc id `<sid>.<plan>` reports every doc "missing"
      (and the truly current ones "stale") - the 212 iter-253 first pass reported 70 missing /
      57 stale where the truth was 13 / 0
Why: the webp file - and the entry's `file` - is named `plan_<plan>.webp`, the site prefix
      STRIPPED (the per-site directory already carries it), while the entry's `fit.doc` keeps the
      full `<site>.<plan>` id. The only correct join is is_done's triple: entry `file` ==
      `plan_<doc.plan>.webp` AND `fit.doc` == `<doc.site>.<doc.plan>` AND `fit.at` == the doc's
      `at` (all three, or a re-built doc whose overlay is not yet synced reads current). Also:
      a platefits doc id built from a glob path must be `os.path.basename(path)[:-5]` - the dir
      prefix breaks the key.

### fit/evidence.py (the evidence contract)

#### check_category re-verifies only the chain's SHAPE - the walk itself is the verification
Where: `fit/evidence.py` (`check_category`); every module that records `kind: category` evidence
      (fit/src_van_deventer.py's cat_chain -> TOWNS["chain"] -> evidence_for)
Symptom: nothing fails: a hand-typed or transformed "via" (a " -> "-joined string, a list that includes the
      file's own category, a chain that skips a hop) passes the offline check, and a picture ends up tied to
      the wrong place
Why: `check_category` only asserts row.cat == site_cat, via[-1] == cat, file_cat not in via - it cannot
      re-walk Commons offline. Record ONLY the actually walked parent list (the JSON a chain walker prints),
      with via[-1] == the site's exact P373 string and the file's category absent from it; a failed walk is
      the caption route or a documented drop, never a guessed chain.

### pipeline/commons.py

#### keep() must be judged AFTER the date/date_commons swap - a post-1925 reproduction of a pre-1925 drawing is dropped otherwise
Where: `pipeline/commons.py` (`keep`, `year_of`, `MAX_YEAR`); `pipeline/sources.py` (`run` - the correct
      order: swap, then gate); `fit/src_van_deventer.py` (`stage` - had the wrong order, fixed 2026-10-11)
Symptom: a staging run raises on a reproduction: "commons.keep() would drop 'File:Plattegrond van J. van
      Deventer, reproductie uit album ... - Sluis - 20201361 - RCE.jpg': fix the table or record the drop" -
      although the byte-same Zwolle done row sits in the canonical files.jsonl (date "circa 1560",
      date_commons "1980")
Why: keep() judges via year_of(title, m), which reads m["date"] (the page/scan date) first. A scan whose page
      date is post-1925 but whose subject is a pre-1925 drawing must be passed the known drawing date FIRST
      (date=want, date_commons=the page value) - sources.py's run() swaps and only then calls keep(), so the
      drawing's year (1560) is what gets judged, not the scan's (1980 > 1925). The done Zwolle row (a 1980 RCE
      album reproduction of a c. 1560 drawing) is the template; any staging module that gates before swapping
      silently drops exactly those reproductions.

#### year_of()/keep() expect m["date"] to be str (or absent) - an int date field crashes them with AttributeError
Where: `pipeline/commons.py` (`year_of`, `keep`, `info`); every staging module doing a Zwolle-style swap (the row's extra dict: `fit/src_us_birdseye.py`, `fit/src_us_birdseye_batch4.py`, `fit/src_us_birdseye_batch5.py`, `fit/src_van_deventer.py`, ...)
Symptom: a staging run dies inside `year_of` with `AttributeError: 'int' object has no attribute 'split'` (the traceback points at `d = raw.split("date QS")[0]`) whenever the row's extra dict passes an int year (e.g. `dict(date=1925)`) instead of a string
Why/fix: `year_of` does `raw = m.get("date") or ""; d = raw.split(...)` - it is written for strings only, and the swap condition evaluates `year_of(title, {"date": want})` before keep(). The known date goes on the row as a STRING (`dict(date="1925")`); the row then carries `date="1925"` (str) and `year=1925` (int, from year_of's return). The batch-5 `indianapolis_1925` row is the template (caught at 241 iteration 178: the landing spec wrote an int; it was changed to a string before staging).
#### A NO-pattern change silently re-drops (or re-keeps) rows already STAGED: commons.rows() re-judges every files.jsonl row with the CURRENT keep(), so the plan list's membership moves when the heuristic moves
Where: `pipeline/commons.py` (`NO`, `keep`, `rows` - the re-judgement); `tools/export_plans.py` (`commons_rows` consumes rows()); `data/commons/files.jsonl` (staged rows); any merge that folds a source's files rows in (211/230)
Symptom: after 230 merged the 18 staged roman files rows, only 1 of them appeared in plans.json: the 17 Horsley rows whose desc ends "leaf nNNNN of the 936-leaf Google scan (British Museum volume)" were dropped by NO's bare `google` (the documented anti-screenshot heuristic), so the 8 new no-QID roman sites' fit panels were empty (2026-10-14, iterations 213-215)
Why: staging gates a row once, but every export re-judges ALL staged rows with the current NO/keep() - a row can pass the stage and still never reach the page. When you refine or extend NO (or any keep() input), re-run tools/export_plans.py and diff the (id, sites[0]) key set against the pre-change file: a lost key means a staged row just flipped. The 230 fix (`google` -> `google (?:maps?|earth|art|street view|satellite)`, with a why-comment at the NO definition) keeps the product-named junk out (Google Maps/Earth/Art Project/Street View/satellite - the 213 GAp drops; src_artists.py:71's rationale) while letting book-scan provenance lines through.

#### Google-book uploads: the djvu XML page number lives in the OBJECT `usemap` attribute, not `data`; per-leaf OCR = the WORDs inside that OBJECT
Where: the `_djvu.xml` of Internet Archive Google uploads (task 208's ORL 1895 volume `derobergermanis00fabrgoog`); `pipeline/books_ia.py` (`page_texts` - hOCR-based, does not apply)
Symptom: `books_ia.page_texts()` yields nothing (these uploads have no `_hocr_searchtext.txt.gz` and their `_djvu.txt` has no form feeds); a regex for the leaf number in `data="..._NNNN.djvu"` matches nothing
Why: Google's djvu XML renders each page as `<OBJECT data="file://…/<id>.djvu" usemap="<id>_NNNN.djvu">` - the leaf number NNNN is in `usemap`, `data` holds the bare djvu name; the per-leaf OCR text is the `<WORD>` elements inside that OBJECT. To map leaves to text for a Google book, parse the OBJECTs by usemap and concatenate their WORDs.

#### validate_book runs fully OFFLINE (socket-blocking safe) once the book's bookreader.json and triage rows are cached - but its `flagged` (site_pages_qwen) silently drops stage-A site pages whose ink is below BLANK_INK

A faded plate that still carries frame/labels/scale bar usually clears 0.005 (Maclauchlan's three site leaves measured 0.0102/0.0352/0.1048 -> all three in, recall_pages 1.0 = stage-A 3/3); a truly blank page at ~0 would not be.

#### Frangi ghost-echoes a ring around razor-sharp synthetic drawings - soften test ink to scan-like edges
Where: `pipeline/autowalls.py` `extract` with its frozen P (sigmas (4,6,9), ridge_thr 0.25, gamma 0.013, coh_sigma 25, min_len/min_extent 50, margin 20); any synthetic-plate test fixture (302c's committed test site, future plate tests)
Symptom: a crisp 0/1 PIL-drawn test plate yields extra skeleton pieces ~5-8 px OUTSIDE the drawn walls (a ghost ring hugging the drawing, even inside the zeroed 20 px margin) in addition to the true centre lines; and an 8 px-wide isolated line blurred to scan-likeness falls below the ridge threshold while the same line at 12 px survives.
Why: gamma 0.013 (the Frangi structuredness scale) is the median default calibrated on real 19th-c. scans, whose edges run a few px of transition and whose paper has texture. A perfect step has a Hessian spectrum that multi-sigma product does not expect: it rings a secondary response a few px outside the step, and softening a thin band drops its response under 0.25. JPEG vs lossless is irrelevant - the ghost is in the drawing, not the codec.
What to do: fixtures should look like scans: 8-12 px wall bands (real plate walls are 6-20 px), gaussian_filter ~2.5 px, a little paper noise (±2/255, fixed rng seed). Verified 2026-10-11 (302a): 8 px rectangle + 12 px interior line, blur 2.5, noise ±2, seed 7 -> exactly the three true centre lines, no ghosts, fully deterministic.
### data/db/platefits (shared fit-doc store)

#### A fit doc naming a site that is not in web/data/sites.json turns test_batch_eu's union checks and test_serve's platefits-docs check red at once
Where: `data/db/platefits/*.json`, `web/data/sites.json`, `fit/batch_eu.py` (`union_check` -> `orphan_docs`), `tests/test_batch_eu.py` (`test_union_check`, `test_union_full_coverage_live`), `tests/test_serve.py` (`test_platefits_docs_match_sites`), `pipeline/build_catalog.py`, `pipeline/build_site.py` (`write_entry`)
Symptom: three new reds from one commit, all in tests the committing task does not own: `assert (not ['<site>.<plan>.json'])` in both batch union tests (orphan_docs) and `assert d["site"] in ids` in the serve test.
Why: the store's invariant is "every fit doc names a built site" (built = an entry in web/data/sites.json). The eu/us partition is region != "US" vs == "US" (batch_eu.eu_sites), so an England build lands in the EU list and its own doc marks it "covered" - building the site breaks nothing else, and the live full-coverage test only skip-gates on the grown population (its "Sites run" number vs the live EU list; 212 re-covers growth). A doc committed before its site is built orphans in all three at once, and the driver counts them as new failures of the committing task. Fix: build the site with the project's own entry point - `.venv/bin/python pipeline/build_catalog.py --ids <sid>` (fetches the DEM; build_site writes the web/data/sites/<id>/ images and appends the sites.json entry via write_entry - the same path plan_fit uses after a fit save; no LiDAR in the box -> the entry's aerial_ok or an old-map cover keeps it, standalone `build_site.py <site.json> --aerial-ok` does the same) - then commit `data/sites/<sid>/site.json` and the sites.json entry (per-site web images, dem.npy, dem_box.json, dem_credit.json are all gitignored and rebuilt by the pipeline) and add both paths to the task's Touches. Do not delete the doc instead: it is the fit's record. 211's merge skips already-built sites (build_catalog skips them), so no stand-in is needed.

#### A fit doc that EXISTS auto-resolves its site's review item (201's derived resolution) - so a 303-refused (kept, unmarked) doc closes the item and the page's Review tab never shows it
Where: `fit/review.py` (`resolved_doc`, `export`), `data/review/README.md` ("Resolution is derived, never a second store"), `tools/site_done.py` (`_sync_doc`'s refusal path), `web/review.js`
Symptom: after a 303 refusal (an unmarked non-auto doc stays in `data/db/platefits/`), the next `review.export` records `resolved: {"doc": ..., "at": ...}` into the item file (write-once) and the item drops out of `web/data/review.json`'s items - the Review tab (open items only) never lists it again, even though the human is supposed to act on the recorded refusal.
Why: 201's contract derives resolution from doc existence alone (a human save is the record; only export writes the `resolved` field), while 303's refusal keeps the doc (no build, no delete). The refusal record survives in the item file (`data/review/<site>.<lead>.json`, candidate `why` = `plan_fit.NO_PROVENANCE`), and once a human places the pairs from the page the PUT stamps `by:hand` and the doc resolves the item for good - the loop closes, the page just doesn't advertise the open middle. 303 conforms to the contract (fit/review.py is not in its Touches; 212/serve rely on it). A fix (e.g. only a doc with a trustworthy `by` resolves) is a 201 contract change: product decision, new task, not a drive-by patch. Verified 2026-10-11 (303 step 3, hermetic: refusal + export recorded resolved and the item left the published queue, second run byte-stable).

#### web/data/review.json is a DERIVED page: change the resolution rules, place/delete fit docs, or add review items without a full `fit/review.py export`, and the committed page goes stale - three count-deriving tests fail on every branch that carries it
Where: `fit/review.py` (`resolved_doc`, `export`), `web/data/review.json`, `data/review/*.json`, `data/db/platefits/`; the tripping tests: `tests/test_fit_provenance.py::test_line_refuses_unmarked_non_auto_doc`, `tests/test_site_done.py::test_site_done_line`, `tests/test_fit_queue.py::test_save_runs_the_one_site_line` (each derives the expected open count from the live page while running the current code in a temp tree)
Symptom: three new reds from one store-related commit, none owned by the committing task, all the same signature: the one-site line / save flow prints "page now has N' open of M items" with N' != the page-derived expectation (2026-10-12: live page 340 open of 341; the runs print 335 / 334 / 334).
Why: a one-site run (`export(root, site_id)`) recomputes the WHOLE page under the current rules but records the write-once `resolved` field only for its own site; a rule change (b22a2d2: a recorded resolution counts only while its document exists) or new/deleted fit docs change which items are excluded, and the committed page keeps advertising them until a FULL export (`site_id=None`) runs: it records the missing resolutions and rewrites the page. A third trigger (2026-10-12, 307ba iteration 119): NEW REVIEW ITEM FILES - every batch run writes data/review/*.json for its unplaceable sites (203a US is already inside the page's 341; agent c's 203b EU batch is in flight), and the page's open/total snapshot goes stale against the grown population exactly like the rule-change case - different numbers than the stale signature, so it reads as new failures on every branch that merges the batch after the last export; the fix is the same full export (item files then byte-identical, only the page rewrites). Fix = full export + commit of the two store paths, done by the task that owns them (220 - the lead ran it themselves as c5250a4 on 2026-10-12, overriding the dep on 309; the page has been in sync since c5250a4, and the third-trigger watch stays armed for items or docs landing after its snapshot); never by re-baselining the three tests - they are correct to fail (the owner's Review tab really shows resolved items) and 803's re-baseline precedent is for tests that PIN a population, which these do not.

#### Merging two branches that both re-exported web/data/review.json conflicts ONLY on the `"at"` line - keep the NEWER timestamp, the item content auto-merges
Where: `web/data/review.json`, any `git merge` in a checkout that has run `fit/review.py export` since the merge base (hit on agent/c vs main, 306d iteration 169)
Symptom: `CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in web/data/review.json` with the sole conflict hunk at lines 2-6: two values of `"at": "<ISO timestamp>"`
Why/fix: every export stamps `at` = now, so both sides always differ there while the items list changes only when both sides added or removed items. When only `at` conflicts (check `git diff <merge-base> <theirs> -- web/data/review.json` - if it shows just that line, the other side re-exported but changed no items): keep the NEWER `at` (the later export reflects the later store state), and the auto-merged item list already carries both sides' additions. If both sides DID change items, union both sides' item intents by hand, then validate: `json.load` the file, count items, and spot-check each side's known additions; a count mismatch means a side's items were lost - run a full `export(root)` (site_id=None) against the merged item files rather than hand-reconciling. Never resolve by keeping only your side: that silently drops the other side's items (their Review tab entries) from the page.

### web/ (the page and its extension scripts)

#### `const x = {}; x = {...}` throws "Assignment to constant variable" at runtime, and a swallowing try/catch turns the crash into silently missing data
Where: page scripts and the headless probe scripts (tests/test_fit_queue.py's PROBE_SCRIPT; fitqueue.js's fqPatch once hit it as `old -> card`)
Symptom: inside a try/catch, no `[pageerror]` at all and the data just loses fields (the card probe's boot came back as `{"ok":true}` with none of its state fields, for 30+ minutes of misdiagnosis); uncaught, Chrome console `[pageerror] Assignment to constant variable.`
Why: reassigning a const is a runtime error, not a parse error - `node --check` and the browser both accept the source; only the assignment itself throws, and a try/catch that exists to tolerate missing page state swallows it without a trace. Use `let` for anything assigned twice, and in a probe, capture `e.message` into the returned object instead of a bare `catch {}`, so a JS bug looks like a JS bug.

#### Two classic <script>s on one page share one global lexical scope: a top-level const/let name may be declared only once across ALL of them
Where: `web/index.html`, `web/review.js`, `web/fitqueue.js` (the extension scripts that save and reassign the page's globals)
Symptom: Chrome console `[pageerror] Identifier '_renderList' has already been declared` (hit by fitqueue.js re-declaring the wrapper-saved names review.js already declared at top level); the second script is rejected WHOLE, so none of what it defines (e.g. the `FQ` queue state, the wrapped `renderList`) exists, and a page probe then fails with `ReferenceError: FQ is not defined` - even though `node --check` on the file passes.
Why: top-level lexical declarations (let/const/class) in a classic script live in the page-wide lexical environment, not a per-script one; only global functions and vars may be re-assigned across scripts. The extension pattern (save the original as `_name`, reassign the global) must therefore pick saved-original names unique per file: review.js took `_renderList`, `_setTabHome`, `_openPlan`, `_saveFit`, `_loadDeps`, and fitqueue.js uses `_fqRenderList` / `_fqSaveFit`. Such a parse error is invisible to `node --check`; only a real browser (the shot.mjs `[pageerror]` line) shows it - smoke every new extension script headless against a served copy before committing.

#### The page's `S` state (any top-level const/let of index.html) is NOT on `window`: a shot.mjs `[js]` probe must use the bare name with a typeof guard
Where: `web/index.html` (the `S` state object, declared top-level `const`), any `tools/shot.mjs` `[js]` probe that reads page state (306a's audit driver polls `S.byId`)
Symptom: `window.S` is `undefined` even on a fully booted page, so a `window.S.byId` guard in a probe reports "site not in S.byId after 30 s" and silently no-ops - while the bare `S.byId` in the very same probe evaluates fine.
Why/fix: a top-level `const`/`let` lives in the page-wide lexical environment, not on globalThis (the entry above): any other script's code - including a string `page.evaluate`d - can reference it by bare name, but `window.<name>` never resolves to it. Write probes as `typeof S !== 'undefined' ? S.byId : null`, never `window.S`.

#### The page's base imagery is a live Esri feed with a SINGULAR `/tile/` path; headless map teardown aborts in-flight tiles (`ERR_ABORTED`) so strict `[reqfail]` assertions red - exclude the host by name, not just `/tiles/`
Where: `web/index.html` (base layer = server.arcgisonline.com World_Imagery; opened per-site since the lead's f5ea863 "aerials listed open" rework); any headless probe that cycles select/startFit/endFit (`tests/test_review.py` PROBE_KEYING, `tests/test_fit_queue.py` card tests)
Symptom: `[reqfail] https://server.arcgisonline.com/ArcGIS/rest/services/World_Imagery/MapServer/tile/Z/X/Y net::ERR_ABORTED` on EVERY run of the affected headless tests, on every branch carrying the page - not a flake and not a network outage (curl from this VM gets HTTP 200, ~15 KB jpeg). The abort is page/probe-caused: the probe's ~100 ms fit cycle tears the map down while tile fetches are in flight, and the browser reports aborted requests as failures. An earlier "ArcGIS flake" diagnosis was wrong on both counts.
Why: World_Imagery tiles take longer than the probe's start/end cycle, so the requests end aborted rather than complete or error. The reqfail check stays strict for every other request; the exclusion must name the host (or the singular `tile/` path) because a `/tiles/` substring filter misses it (309/221, iteration 111).

#### The home stats line is matched by a two-wording regex (`built in all|laid on today`) - any code or test that finds it must accept both wordings
Where: `web/review.js:74` and `web/fitqueue.js:56` (the page's own matchers, which anchor `#rvcount` / the card into that line), `web/index.html:588` (the line), `tests/test_review.py` test_page_shows_the_review_list
Symptom: a consumer pinned to one wording (201's test filtered the substring "built in all") stops finding the line after a re-word - "the home stats line must be present" fails on every branch, while the page's own feature still works (its matcher accepts both wordings).
Why: the lead re-worded the line in 939382a ("...laid on today's ground...") and both page matchers already accept the disjunction. The page's regex is the source of truth: mirror it (either wording), never re-pin one - the wording may move again in 307's page rework.

#### web/data/sites/<site>/ survey layers (etatmajor, cassini, tmk1850, fr_ortho1950) are site-sized georeferenced blocks - 1 px = 1 m for sites up to 2400 m across
Where: `pipeline/depict.py` (`build`: `aw.site_bbox` + `px = max(1.0, max(width_m, height_m)/2400)` + `sample_xyz`/
      `sample_rd`); the `web/data/sites/<site>/*.webp` files and their `depictions.json` `corners`; the source
      records `data/sites/<id>/site.json`
Symptom: treating `etatmajor.webp` (or a sibling survey layer) as a zoom-level tile or a variable sheet - it is a
      fixed box: the site's width_m x height_m centred on the site's own lon/lat, resampled to width_m/px x
      height_m/px pixels (cenabum's 1600 m box -> a 1600 x 1600 px file)
Why: for sites whose max dimension is <= 2400 m, px = 1.0, so 1 px = 1 m and the image centre is the site point;
      the `corners` in depictions.json are the block's [lon, lat] corners, so any crop is exactly georeferenced.
      That makes these files ideal local ground truth for judging a fit (task 306b): crop the region, measure in
      pixels, 1 px = 1 m, and the printed survey ink (the 1850s etatmajor town names) verifies a placement with no
      network.

#### Driving the fit tool headlessly with your own pairs: a fitqueue entry for the opened plan seeds 5 anchor pairs into your least squares
Where: `web/fitkit.js` (`_fkActivate` seeds the entry's 5 anchor pairs when the opened plan matches an entry in
      `web/data/fit_queue.json`); any headless audit that pushes its own pairs through `openPlan` + `refit`
      (task 306b's `tools/audit_306b.mjs`; the 306c-f orphan audits)
Symptom: the fitted preview (the fit-prev map source, the fithint m/px) reflects a 13-point blend (5 seed + 8 your)
      instead of your 8-point fit - silently, no pageerror; the transform you judge is not the document's
Why/fix: after `startFit` and before `openPlan`, wait for `FQ.loaded` and empty `FQ.entries` in the page context

#### web/data/sites/<site>/depictions.json is a DICT {"depictions": [...]}, not a bare list
Where: `web/data/sites/<id>/depictions.json` (the page's depiction list); overlay-membership scanners (the 306a/b/c audits)
Symptom: iterating the loaded file yields the string keys, so `d.get("fit")` crashes with AttributeError on a str - the 306c inventory scanner's first crash

#### The page's LiDAR is the per-site prebuilt relief.jpg, mapped LINEARLY onto the site corners (image px -> lon/lat) - the reliable way to read a real work's position without the live tile service
Where: `web/index.html` (`ensureSite` L367-368), `web/data/sites/<id>/relief.jpg`, `web/data/sites.json` (`corners`)
Symptom/need: `/tiles/relief/*` is off on this VM (aw is Mac-only), so the only LiDAR the page - and any audit of it - sees is the per-site relief.jpg raster stretched over the site corners rect; to judge a fit you need the real work's coordinates off that raster
Why: the mapping is linear (image px -> corners interpolation, no projection), so it inverts exactly: site point -> image px, or a feature's image px -> site point. That is how 306c pinned the serpent effigy (head (-83.4288, 39.0254), tail (-83.4314, 39.0258)) and the pyramid-mound's ~100 m dark-ringed mound at ~(-87.5056, 38.6705) - one from the committed audit shots' map panes, the other straight off the committed 800x800 relief.jpg (1 px = 1.00 m for that site). No network, no live tiles.

#### On the 1842 six-inch *_ink.webp individual standing stones do not resolve (~666 px over the 800 m box); for stone-circle sites the LiDAR relief's dark dots are the deciding layer
Where: `web/data/sites/<site>/six-inch-1st_ink.webp`, `web/data/sites/<site>/relief.jpg`; 306e's stone-circle audits (stanton-drew, iteration 194)
Symptom: zooming the 1842 six-inch's "Druidical Circles" dot cluster smears it into blobs and hachure at any magnification - the cluster's location and extent are readable, but any "how many / how big are the real circles" measurement off the six-inch ink comes out over-broad
Why/how: the webp is only 666 px over the site's 800 m box (~1.2 m/px), so 1-2 m stones are sub-pixel and merge with the surrounding hachure/field ink. The relief.jpg shows each stone as a distinct dark dot on the local bright field (stanton-drew: the real cluster reads as ~50 m of dots at E+100..150 N-50, which the drawn 435 m ring only surrounds). For stone-circle/standing-stone sites, judge the drawn circles against the relief's dark dots (a local window, threshold ~ median-25) and use the 1842 for the cluster's location and the printed labels only.

#### MapLibre marker elements are parked at the canvas origin by the vendor css and placed only by their inline transform - a page rule with a flowing position (relative) that loads after the vendor link re-enters the marker into normal flow and lands it 500-3000px off its site
Where: `web/index.html` (`.marker` / `.ah` / `.tag` css, `addMarkers` / `syncMarkers`) + `web/vendor/maplibre-gl-5.6.0.css` (`.maplibregl-marker { left: 0; position: absolute; top: 0 }`)
Symptom: most markers missing in globe view (61/324 in-view instead of 324/324); for the visible ones the measured rect's bottom-centre minus the marker's inline transform point is a large, VARYING offset (505-3023px) instead of a constant; markers that should be out of view get pushed in by the flow offset (Orkney showed up, Wiltshire dropped out).
Why: MapLibre parks the marker element at the canvas origin and places it purely with the inline transform (`translate(-50%,-100%) translate(Xpx,Ypx)`). A page rule with equal-or-higher specificity that loads after the vendor `<link>` (for 308, `.marker { ...; position: relative }`, both 0,1,0 - the inline `<style>` wins the cascade tie) puts each marker back into normal flow, stacking it below the previous one in DOM order. Found while building 308's arrowheads; the initial "globe projection" reading (transform = on-globe position, `map.project()` = flat plane, 3023px apart) was a MISDIAGNOSIS of this bug: transform and `map.project()` agree within 0.35px. (Separate, informational: in globe mode the canvas container is larger than the viewport - 1440x3038 at 1440x900.)
How to avoid: restate `position: absolute; top: 0; left: 0;` in the page's `.marker` rule (a comment there explains why a flowing position must not be used). The acceptance check: rect bottom-centre minus the transform point must be a small CONSTANT (= the anchor geometry; 0 for the borderless `.ah` box) and the in-view count must match the pre-change baseline.

#### A pin that syncMarkers holds back or that is off screen is DETACHED from the page - `document.querySelectorAll('.marker')` finds only the shown pins (plus the open site's)
Where: `web/index.html` (`syncMarkers` / `setOff`, `markers` array); any probe or test that counts or looks up `button.marker` elements
Symptom: a probe that finds a site's pin by `[...document.querySelectorAll('button.marker')]` returns null for a pin that is zoom-gated, decluttered or outside the view; counting `.marker[data-off]` gives ~0 instead of the hundreds it used to
Why/how: MapLibre moves every attached marker on every frame (533 attached cost ~8 ms a frame on a fast desktop, ~25 ms on a 4x-throttled phone), so since the perf pass (2026-10-29) a hidden pin leaves the map (`Marker.remove()`) and comes back when shown. The open site's own pin stays attached (hidden by `data-off`) because test_owner_check reads its class. To reach every pin use the page's `markers` array (bare name in page.evaluate, typeof guard): `markers.find(k => k.id === id).el`.

#### Every web/data/sites `*_ink.webp` survey layer is a SURVEY-RED overlay: the ink lives in the ALPHA channel only - every pixel's RGB is the constant colour (206,46,78)
Where: `pipeline/depict.py` (`make_ink`, `add_ink`), `pipeline/build_site.py` (`plate_ink`, `INK = (206, 46, 78)`); the `web/data/sites/<site>/six-inch-1st_ink.webp`, `os1inch_ink.webp`, `tmk1850_ink.webp`, ... files (gitignored shared build output)
Symptom: a "dark ink" mask recipe (e.g. `alpha>40 & rgb.sum()<300`) applied to a `_ink.webp` finds ZERO pixels - the rgb of every non-transparent pixel sums to ~330
Why/how: `make_ink` stamps the constant INK (206,46,78) into the RGB of every pixel and puts the plate-ink darkness into the alpha channel, so alpha is the only per-pixel information. The ink mask is `a>40` (measured on the 1842 six-inch of okehampton-castle and old-sarum, 2026-10-13, 306e iteration 181); a hatched/wood band is the dilated mask `uniform_filter(ink, 15) > 0.06`. See also the companion entry on compositing these files.

#### An `*_ink.webp`'s TRANSPARENT pixels carry the ink colour as RGB - a plain `.convert("RGB")` crop comes out solid pink; composite through the alpha channel
Where: any audit script reading `web/data/sites/<site>/*_ink.webp` (306d/306e's /tmp composites); PIL `.convert("RGB")` on RGBA input
Symptom: cropping a `_ink.webp` region and `.convert("RGB")`-ing it yields a uniformly pink (206,46,78) image instead of "ink on paper" - the ink appears everywhere, because the RGB of the "empty" pixels is the ink colour, only their alpha is 0
Why/how: the files are built as constant-RGB + alpha (the entry above). To composite one over a background (relief grey, a plate paper, another layer), paste through the alpha channel - `Image.composite(fg, bg, fg.getchannel("A"))` or `bg.paste(fg, box, fg)` - or work in `getchannel("A")` alone for masks. Never `convert("RGB")` a crop for measuring or drawing.

#### Inverting the page's simFit (mercator -> plate px): u = (q0*a0 + q1*a1)/a2, v = (q0*a1 - q1*a0)/a2 with a2 = a0^2 + a1^2 (v = -Im); a wrong v sign lands the plate ink as a mirrored ghost
Where: `web/index.html` (`simFit` at L1004; `merc` at L360 - TRUE Mercator, y = R*ln(tan(pi/4 + lat*pi/360)), NOT R*angle); any audit that inverse-maps the page's stored fit (306d/306e's /tmp composites)
Symptom: the composite's plate-ink overlay (blue, sampled through the inverse) lands mirrored or offset - e.g. zero blue ink over the site grid or a left-right mirror of the drawing - while the page's own rendering of the same pairs looks correct
Why/how: simFit solves z = a*w + b with w = u - i*v (image v-axis points DOWN, complex convention) and a complex a (a0 + i*a1); the inverse is w = (z - b)/a, and division by a complex number conjugates the denominator, giving u = (q0*a0 + q1*a1)/a2 and v = (q0*a1 - q1*a0)/a2 for q = z - b. A sign slip in v (writing +a1 where -a1 belongs, or the like) mirrors the plate. Verify any inversion BEFORE trusting a composite: the 4 stored anchor pairs must round-trip, atv(at(u,v)) = (u,v) to ~1e-9.

#### Merging main after your branch re-exported web/data/review.json: the conflict is usually only the "at" line, but the auto-merged items list must be VERIFIED, never trusted on sight
Where: `web/data/review.json`, any `git merge main` in a checkout that ran `fit/review.py export` since the merge base (recurred 306e iteration 187 - agent/c vs main: my 306c/d/e item additions against main's 234 no-picture re-stamps; first hit 306d iteration 169)
Symptom: `CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in web/data/review.json` with the sole conflicting hunk on the `"at": "<ISO timestamp>"` line, even though BOTH sides changed items - when the sides added or re-stamped different items the items-list lines do not textually overlap, so git auto-merges them into a union while only `at` conflicts
Why/fix: every export stamps `at` = now, so that line always differs; keep the NEWER `at` (the later export reflects the later store state). But a line-level union of a hand-written JSON list is exactly the kind of merge that can silently drop or duplicate an item (a lost item line = a lost site's Review tab entry), so verify the resolution instead of assuming it: `json.load` the merged file, count its items against both parents, and spot-check each side's known additions. If the count does not match, do not hand-reconcile - run a full `fit/review.py export` (site_id=None) against the merged item files; the page file is derived from data/review/ and that regenerates it correctly. Never resolve by keeping only your side: that silently drops the other side's items.

#### The page can only fetch files under web/data/*: /data/ URLs are served from web/ (serve.py directory=WEB), so the store's data/review items and data/db docs are NOT fetchable from the page - a probe that fetch()s them gets 404 on every poll
Where: `server/serve.py` (`WEB = ROOT/web`, the static handler `directory=WEB`, so GET `/data/...` maps to `<tree>/web/data/...`); any headless probe that verifies server-side effects through the page (tests/test_owner_check.py's effects poll); the page's own scripts (they fetch only depictions.json / sites.json / review.json / relief tiles)
Symptom: a `page.evaluate` that does `fetch('data/review/<item>.json?t=')` (or `data/db/platefits/...`) gets HTTP 404 on EVERY fetch - visible as a 404 in the server access log on each poll second, with no transient phase. `web/data/` has no `review/` or `db/` subdirectory in the checkout or in the private test trees: the item files live only in the store's `data/review/` and the docs only in `data/db/platefits/`, neither of which is ever served (hit by 307d, iteration 248: the poll's item fetch 404'd all 120 s, and the unassigned `state` cascaded into every dependent check, including the reload check)
Why/fix: verify store-side effects (an item's `resolved`, a doc's bytes) from the tree on the PYTHON side of the test, never through the page. Ordering is safe when the writer does it: `fit/review.py export` writes `resolved` into the item file BEFORE it writes `web/data/review.json`, so a poll that returns ok only once the site is gone from the page file has the resolution on disk already. Cache headers differ by type (`serve.py end_headers`): every `*.json` is `no-cache`, but non-json `/data/*` and `/vendor/*` are `max-age=3600` - in-page polls should still append `?t=` on every fetch: it costs nothing on the no-cache files and is the only way to see a rebuilt image.

#### saveFit's one-shot sites.json fetch could land in the ~119 ms depiction->re-score gap and adopt the PRE-rescore tier; a longer poll on the probe side cannot fix it - 245 made the adoption a bounded re-fetch loop keyed on `overlays` growing
Where: `web/index.html` (`saveFit`: polls `depictions.json` every 1.5 s, and when the saved depiction appears, fetches `sites.json` and adopts drawings/score/oldest/overlays + sets the marker class from that one fetch, then stops); the one-site line `server/serve.py _fit_worker -> tools/site_done.py` (writes depictions.json 01:57:23.310, then re-scores and rewrites sites.json :23.429 - 119 ms later); `tests/test_owner_check.py` B probe step "line effect (b): the site's square takes its new score's tier"
Symptom: after saving a fit whose score crosses a tier boundary, the site's square keeps its OLD class on screen (`marker t1` instead of the new `marker t2`; score 1.1 -> 1.45) until a manual reload - the persisted data is correct (the reload section of the same probe reads t2), and the probe's 120 s effects poll never sees the change, red'ing the owner_check pair at that step, per-save (A's poll landed after the re-score, B's in the gap)
Why: the one-site line builds the overlay FIRST (depictions.json gains the entry) and re-scores the site SECOND (`build_site.set_drawings` computes the score FROM the built overlays, so the order is mandatory - never reorder the pipeline to "fix" a tier race); a 1.5 s-poll fetch landing in the 119 ms gap between the two writes adopts the pre-rescore score, and saveFit adopted only from that ONE fetch. A longer poll on the probe side cannot un-adopt a one-shot adoption. Fix (245, ab57da1b): the one-shot fetch is now a bounded re-fetch loop (8 x 250 ms) that adopts the fetched fields each time and breaks once the fetched entry's `overlays` exceeds the pre-save in-memory value (a new depiction = +1 overlay); a missing `overlays` on either side keeps the old single-fetch behaviour. Verified it.236 (2026-10-15): pre-fix pair run A green / B red at exactly this step; post-fix 3 consecutive pair runs green (64-67 s, "new score's tier" [ok] in every run, zero [warn] settle), cross-run all ten views 0.000% differing (PIL per-channel threshold 32).

### tests/playwright

#### page.evaluate callbacks run in the BROWSER: there is no fs/process/module scope there - do Node-side reads outside the evaluate and pass the values in as arguments
Where: any playwright test whose probe does file I/O (tests/test_owner_check.py's effects evaluate called `readFileSync` inside `page.evaluate` despite a top-level `import { readFileSync } from 'fs'` in the .mjs)
Symptom: `ReferenceError: readFileSync is not defined` thrown from the evaluate's first statement on every run; with a try/catch around the poll, the crash degrades to a silent `{ok: false, state: {}}` after the poll timeout, which misdirects every downstream check (307d run 2: both saves had completed perfectly on the server, yet all four line-effect checks and the reload check failed against the empty state)
Why/fix: `page.evaluate` serializes the callback into the page's V8 and runs it with no Node module scope; only its arguments cross the bridge. Read the file on the Node side first (try/catch -> null if the write may still be pending - the poll can time out before the server-side write lands), pass the parsed value into the evaluate as an argument, and let the Python side do any comparison that needs the real file.

#### A JS string literal inside a Python raw string needs ONE backslash before an embedded quote (`\'`); two (`\\'`) write an escaped backslash into the .mjs, the quote closes the string, and node dies with a SyntaxError at import
Where: probe .mjs sources held as Python raw strings (tests/test_owner_check.py's PROBE; the 307bb template tests/test_fit_queue.py's probe dodged this by keeping apostrophes in `//` comments only)
Symptom: both tests die in ~1.7 s at the ESM import, before any page boots (307d runs 1-2, node 22): a `SyntaxError` at the probe line of the first possessive - `site\\'s own` in the .mjs parses as `site\` + string-closing quote + the bare identifier `s`; `node --check` on the extracted probe fails identically
Why/fix: in a Python raw string what you type is what the .mjs gets: `\\` is two backslashes = one JS-escaped backslash, so the quote that follows CLOSES the string. Type ONE backslash (`\'` in the .py source) for the JS escape. Gate every probe change with `node --check` on the regenerated .mjs (10 s) before spending minutes on a browser run.

#### test_owner_check's ten 307d PNGs are a PINNED SNAPSHOT (the 242 split, merged): an unflagged run leaves them byte-identical (the write-surface proof hashes all ten); only AW_OWNER_REFRESH=1 re-renders them - history: before 813 EVERY run re-rendered them into docs/site_flow/ without diffing, the PNG encoding is machine-specific and not fully deterministic run-to-run, so a branch that ran the suite was dirty on them and merges conflicted (b14918f)

Where: tests/test_owner_check.py::test_owner_save_site_size_fallback (runs _run_one(fx, "B"): check 6 `open_sites == reviewBefore - {B, A.site}` and the "B's run rewrote A's already-resolved item file" assert both assume A's run resolved A's site first), the module-scoped owner_served fixture (one shared private tree for both tests)

It is agent a's test (307d's Touches); if it fails again, first make sure A ran first in the same invocation before suspecting anything else. 2026-10-14 on agent a's 230 checkout the pair was RED 3 times in a row (it.214 full suite, it.215 pair, it.216 pair) at the A probe step "toolbar scale and turn change the drawing on screen" (pick richard-s-castle-q17650937 / earthworkenglan01allcgoog_n0453_1) even though every relevant file (site dirs, fit_queue.json, review.json, 71 platefits, Chrome binary) is byte-identical to main and agent c's checkout - a machine-state flake (render not settled at the before/after shot; hypothesis: GPU contention from the parallel agents' concurrent test runs perturbing headless-browser render timing - the same mid-transition signature 242 measured on the saved/reload PNGs). The stability fix (settle before shooting) is the 242 split: 814 does the settle wait, 812 the in-run double-shot assert, 813 the pinned-snapshot regime (all merged to main); 810, 811 and 242 carried the waits (242 is now the final-verification gate).

#### test_owner_check probe logs: a GREEN pair run rmtree's the whole pytest basetemp at session end (pytest.ini: retention policy "failed", count 1 - the pytest section above), and the B-side log's window is only ~1 s, so a 0.5-1 s poll misses it - capture with a 0.1 s watcher started BEFORE pytest
Where: tests/test_owner_check.py::_run_one (writes outdir/owner_probe.log = the probe's full stdout+stderr right after each node probe returns, then asserts on it); the logs live at $TMPDIR/pytest-of-agent/pytest-<N>/owner{A,B}0/owner_probe.log (pytest 9 nests the session dir one level under the basetemp root); agent a's rig /tmp/loop-ancient-works.a/814-verify/ (watchlogs.py + runpair.sh - /tmp trees do not survive session boundaries: the /tmp-persistence entry in this file)
Symptom: after a green pair run, a basetemp poll at 0.5 s (or 1 s, the 194 recipe) catches only A's log; B's log (written when B's probe returns, seconds before session end) is gone - 814 it.242: missed twice at 0.5 s; every green run left pytest-of-agent/ completely empty (reproduced with a 1-test throwaway: 0.59 s run, wiped before the first ls after exit)
Why: A's log has a wide window (B's whole test duration, ~35 s), but B's window is only the python-side checks after B's probe (~1 s: the one-site-line finished-report wait + the tree reads) before the green-session rmtree
What to do: start a 0.1 s os.walk watcher over $TMPDIR/pytest-of-agent BEFORE launching pytest; on first sight of any owner_probe.log copy it out (skip pytest-<N> dirs that predate the run; re-queue the key if the copy races the wipe). A 0.1 s poll caught A@+36.8 s and B@+69.8 s of a 69.7 s run. On a RED run the basetemp survives (the failed policy) and a post-exit sweep suffices. A test's end-to-end pass already proves its probe's checks passed (a red probe fails the test via the RESULT assert); the only evidence only the log carries is [warn] settle lines and the ratio check's [ok]. One watcher must NOT span consecutive runs: after each green wipe the session-dir numbering restarts at pytest-0, so a relpath-only key collides across runs and a later run's log is silently skipped (816 it.243: a single watcher across four pair runs lost run 2's A+B logs; a fresh watcher with its own dest dir per run caught every log). If one watcher must span runs, add the session dir's mtime to the key. The copy-out key must be FLATTENED (`os.path.relpath(root, base).replace(os.sep, "_")`): with a relpath key like `pytest-0/ownerA0` the destination `<dest>/pytest-0/ownerA0.log` has a non-existent parent dir, `shutil.copy2` raises FileNotFoundError and a wipe-race `except FileNotFoundError` silently swallows it - every capture fails forever with zero output (814 it.244: a run-4 watcher with an unflattened key lost BOTH logs of a 67 s run; the identical os.walk logic printed correct results in the foreground, so the only symptom is a silent no-catch - check the watcher's own stdout, and test it against a hand-created file before trusting it on a real run).

#### test_owner_check settle: isMoving() goes false while frames are still rendering (up to ~1.5 s past the ease on the globe projection) - the 812 in-run double shot catches that straggler; the gate is camera-at-rest PLUS ~700 ms of render-quiet (hooked on the live map, window.__awLastRender)
Where: tests/test_owner_check.py probe `settle` (814's `!map.isMoving()` gate + 812's additive render-quiet gate); `shot()` takes `<name>.png` then `<name>b.png` and Python's `_shot_diff` asserts <0.5% at threshold 32 in `_run_one`
Symptom: the in-run double-shot pair differs even though the settle returned: it.245 run 4 - B 2-placed 0.9944%, B 5-reload 0.5267% (frame-wide, bbox x[0,1279] y[0,819]; BOTH probe logs said RESULT PASS - a residual drift/re-tile after the ease, not a check failure). In the same session a pre-widen run red'd both tests (details lost to the next session's basetemp wipe)
Why: MapLibre 5.6.0's isMoving() tracks only the camera animation (_prepareEase/_easeEnd); on the globe projection tile render/re-tile runs ~1.5 s past isMoving() false (it.235's /tmp/mplib_probe: isMoving true until ~8 s, render/data events until ~9.5 s, then ONE idle and the event count froze for 20 s - the render loop is event-driven). The 814 re-claim (999e5bf3) pre-dates the double-shot proof, so its "0 [warn]" green runs could carry exactly this straggler - it only dirtied the PNGs, which R5 restores invisibly
What to do: the widened settle (landed with 812 on agent/a, it.245): settle waits `!map.isMoving() && Date.now() - window.__awLastRender > 700`, where the probe hooks `map.on('render')` on the live map at first use - the window state is fresh after a page.reload() so the hook re-registers, and the served tree stays untouched. Five consecutive green pair runs after the widen: all in-run double shots 0.0000%, zero [warn] settle, cross-run 9/10 byte-identical (worst B 1-card 0.0447%, the known card band). If a double-shot assert fails again: first widen the quiet window (never weaken the 0.5% line) and record the failing view in DECISIONS.
#### The runpair script's backgrounded poller subshell survives session teardown as an orphan (PPID 1) and keeps scanning $TMPDIR/pytest-of-agent forever - check `ps` at session start and kill stragglers
Where: the runpair script's `( while true; do find $TMPDIR/pytest-of-agent -name owner_probe.log; ...; sleep 1; done ) &` poller (bash -c, tests/test_owner_check.py pair runs); this lane's TMPDIR /tmp/loop-ancient-works.c
Symptom: no pytest process is running, yet `ps -ef | grep owner_probe.log` shows `bash -c ... owner_probe.log` processes with PPID 1 and a live `sleep 1` child - 815 it.212: two such loops from a previous session (started 05:00/05:03, their pytests finished at 05:01/05:04, both `2 passed`) were still looping at 08:32 - the script's own `kill $POLLER` line never reached them, because session teardown killed the OUTER bash -c first and re-parented the subshell to init
Why: a `&`-backgrounded subshell is not in the outer script's foreground process group, so a teardown that takes out the outer script (or the harness's whole process tree by group) orphans it rather than killing it; only nohup'd children are documented to survive (the run_build entry), but plain `&` subshells do too
What to do: at session start (the orient step) `ps -ef | grep owner_probe.log | grep -v grep` and kill any PIDs found; they are mostly harmless (read-only find + `cp -n` into a stale /tmp dest dir - they can never corrupt a current run's capture, which has its own watcher and dest, and `cp -n` never overwrites) but they are noise and their stale dest dirs make later log archaeology confusing

Where: `tests/test_matchfit_station.py` (`_drift` recomputes `record.py::_input_hashes()` against the live repo and compares it to the fixture's `header.input_hashes` - 9 whole-row sha256s: hand_doc, plan_image, site_dir, sites_entry, plans_row, index_row, catalog_row, site_json, data_review); `tests/fixtures/matchfit_station/records.json` + `records_unsure.json` (header: recorded_at + input_hashes); `data/books/index.jsonl`
