### data/merge/ (211's consolidation runners)

#### run_build.py is nohup'd, survives session teardown, and is one site per child - never start a second one for overlapping ids
Where: data/merge/run_build.py (the box-3 site runner), data/merge/build_sites.log (append-only run log)
Symptom: a previous session's `nohup .venv/bin/python data/merge/run_build.py <ids> &` is still running (`ps aux | grep run_build`); the log's last `=== <sid> start` has no `build rc=` tail yet; a second instance for the same ids would race it on web/data/sites.json
Why: ending a session does not kill the detached process; each site is one `pipeline/build_catalog.py --ids <sid>` subprocess, so a kill leaves a clean boundary at the last finished site, and build_catalog skips already-built sites, so resuming with the remaining ids is always safe.
What to do: before launching anything, check `ps`. Log semantics: `NOT BUILT: <sid>` = the machinery skipped it (no LiDAR and no old map, or the id matched no catalog row - sids include the Q-id, so a typo'd id like `vieille-hesdin` silently builds nothing); `=== <sid> FAILED ===` = the subprocess exited non-zero (traceback logged above it). The per-site `marks refreshed` line is build_site.set_drawings on that one site only.

#### A driver merge can add new site entries to web/data/sites.json that this checkout never built - test_merge reds until you build them HERE, and `--force` zeroes the marker fields (restore the committed file after)
Where: `web/data/sites.json`, `web/data/sites/<id>/` (gitignored), `data/sites/<id>/site.json` (tracked), `pipeline/build_catalog.py` (`--ids`, `--force`), `tests/test_merge.py` (`test_new_sites_are_complete`), the driver's "[driver] merge main into agent/<x>" commits
Symptom: straight after the driver merges main, `test_merge.py::test_new_sites_are_complete` fails with `<sid>: no web/data/sites directory` for every site whose entry arrived in the merge (2026-10-15, 241: the nine Roman sites ardoch/carriden/cilurni/congavata/kirkintilloch/luguvallium-q71551754/petriana/tunnocelum/virosidum from 230's re-run) - deterministic on that checkout, not a flake: the per-site directories are local build artifacts that never travel in git, and a long-lived checkout is missing exactly the ones it never built itself (the main checkout lacked all nine too - the reference build lives in the checkout that did the building, here agent a's)
Why/fix: build them with the project's own entry point: `.venv/bin/python pipeline/build_catalog.py --ids <sids> --force` (the ids must exist in data/catalog/sites.jsonl + extras.jsonl; the fetches are live - EA WCS, srsp-open-data S3, NLS mapseries-tilesets S3 - all reachable from this machine; nine sites took about five minutes). The build is deterministic: 241's rebuild came out byte-identical to the reference build in agent a's checkout (cmp -s over every file) and the tracked site.json inputs regenerated byte-identical. The only tracked file the run dirties is web/data/sites.json - `--force` rewrites the rebuilt sites' marker fields (score/oldest/overlays) to zero because the build_catalog path does not recompute them (the consolidating task's --marks pass stamps the committed values) - so `git checkout -- web/data/sites.json` afterwards. The committed markers describe exactly what the freshly built local directories contain, so restoring the committed bytes leaves the checkout consistent and green (test_merge 10/10). The fix is per-checkout: any other checkout that never built those sites shows the same red.

### A/B-testing a change against a pristine tree (in-checkout, never a fresh worktree)

#### A/B in this project must run in your own checkout with the changed files temporarily at HEAD - a fresh worktree at HEAD lacks the locally-built site data and fails 3 tests that pass in the main checkout
Where: any A/B of a data change (306c/306d orphan removals, agent a's 222-228), `git worktree add`, `web/data/sites/` (only 58 of 389 site dirs are git-tracked; the rest, plus `data/raw/`, are local build artifacts that never travel in git), `tests/test_site_done.py`, `tests/test_fit_provenance.py`, `tests/test_fit_queue.py`
Symptom: a fresh worktree at HEAD fails exactly 3 tests that pass in the main checkout: `site_done_line` with FileNotFoundError `<worktree>/web/data/sites/stonehenge-q39671`, `test_fit_provenance.py::test_line_refuses_unmarked_non_auto_doc`, `test_fit_queue.py::test_save_runs_the_one_site_line` - and any test that reads a locally-built per-site file or a raw image sees "missing" files that exist in the other checkouts, so an A/B done there cannot attribute a failure to the change or to the missing build artifacts.
Why/fix: the per-site web data and data/raw were built locally in the main checkout and never entered git, so a worktree checkout of any commit is structurally incomplete. The idiom (proven by 306d iteration 162 and agent a's 224): in YOUR checkout, run the test selection with your changed files temporarily restored to HEAD (`git checkout -- <files>`, or keep your versions in a /tmp dir), record pass/fail per test, then re-apply your change and re-run the SAME selection; failures identical in both states are pre-existing, failures only with your change are yours. It is a few minutes, not a session. (Learned 2026-10-13: my first 306d A/B used a /tmp worktree and was invalid for exactly this reason.)
### tools/export_plans.py

#### A plans.json row exists only on machines that hold the picture's local copy - re-exports grow and shrink by environment, not by data
Where: tools/export_plans.py (`commons_rows`: skips a row without `data/raw/commons/<site>/<sha16(title)>.jpg`; the books branch skips an index row without its `full_local` page image), web/data/plans.json; consumers: 212's sync (fit/cover.py `_regen_plans`), test_merge, test_fit_queue, the page's plan list
Symptom: the same files.jsonl/classified.jsonl content exported on two machines yields different plans.json (lead's Mac f970500: 1474 rows without numancia's c_0fa271e2444f7bfc; this VM's re-export: 1168 rows with numancia and byte-identical to 953d9ab, missing the 307 rows the Mac had - measured 2026-10-13, task 212/233)
Why: data/raw is gitignored per-machine; a picture (commons or books) reaches the plan list only where a local copy of it exists. So a re-export can DROP rows another machine put in (that copy is missing here) and ADD rows it lacks (the fetch phase fills them first - 212's fetch runs before its re-export on purpose).
What to do: after any plans.json regeneration, diff the (id, sites[0]) key set against the previous file; an expected pure-growth diff (new local copies, no losses) is normal, a lost key means a fetch failure (or a row that no longer passes the classified thresholds) - record it as a data finding, do not re-add the row by hand.

### tools/site_done.py, fit/review.py

#### A batch re-run of a review-item row replaces that candidate's entry whole - site_done's skip guard is the only thing protecting audit notes
Where: fit/review.py `upsert_item` (candidates merge by `plan`: a same-plan entry REPLACES the existing one in place), fit/batch_us.py `run_sites`/`_entry` (writes plain {plan, title, url, evidence, pairs, why} entries), tools/site_done.py `fit` (re-fits only rows with NEITHER a doc NOR a review-item entry)
Symptom: a site whose item carries rich per-candidate notes silently loses them - any run that re-fits those rows overwrites the entry with the batch's plain shape. Measured 2026-10-13 (task 212): bethlehem's 22-candidate item and shotwick's 2-candidate item carry 306a audit fields (coarse/ground/rot_deg/scale_m_px/note + specific why strings) and survive ONLY because every one of their rows is already an item candidate, so site_done's fit() finds no uncovered row and never calls run_sites.
Why: the item's candidate list is the last writer's output per plan; batch_us.run_sites upserts unconditionally for whatever rows it is given, and only site_done's one-site line feeds it rows that could already be in the item. site_done's docstring documents the skip ("a blind re-run would swap" the entries).
What to do: if you add a runner that re-fits rows already present in an item, preserve or merge the existing entry's fields first (or move audit detail out of the candidate entry); tests that pin audit whys (the 306 series, 231/232) depend on the skip staying as-is.

#### A fully-hatched bird's-eye plate defeats ink-threshold measurement: the hatched ground reads as strong ink, so annulus/farthest-ink radii saturate and no drawn ring radius can be isolated
Where: the 306-series fit audit that measures a fitted plate's drawn works (the luminance-alpha plate-ink mask `alpha = clip((170-L)*1.9, 0, 255)` used to composite and measure a Commons plate, e.g. the /tmp/aw306e_* scripts)
Symptom: for a densely hatched plate (measured 2026-10-13 on Ditchfield 1901's 'Ichnography', old-sarum c_041083ec68b532f8, 686x892), a strong-ink mask (alpha>120) covers ~34% of the plate and its radial annulus density is flat (~10/px out to the box edge); 'farthest ink per azimuth' then hits the rmax cap in every direction, so the drawn ring's radius comes back as a number that is just the search bound, not the ring.
Why: the stippled/hatched ground inside and around the drawn ring is as dark as the ring line itself, so a luminance threshold cannot separate the line from the fill; only a clean line drawing (thin pen work on white, like the Basire plan) thresholdes into a measurable ring.
What to do: for a dense plate, do NOT read drawn radii off an ink histogram or a per-azimuth farthest-ink scan. Read them off the 800 m box grid composite (100 m grid + 100-500 m circles centred on the site point, /tmp/aw306e_osarum_grid.py) or the fitted aerial/relief screenshots (docs/site_flow/agent_fits/), where the drawn complex is over the real ground and its size against the 1842 ink and LiDAR is visible directly. Reserve ink-threshold measurement for clean line drawings.

#### web/data/review.json is a full re-export of data/review/ - re-deriving it after a branch merge is safe (even though a commit message can say "item files byte-identical")
Where: fit/review.py `export`/`upsert_item`, web/data/review.json, data/review/*.json (the 212a no-picture re-stamps: 9c48d94; its export phase a7f5dda)
Symptom: after merging main, web/data/review.json has a merge conflict (the `at` timestamp, because both branches are full re-exports); a commit message like a7f5dda's ("234 no-picture items re-stamped ... item files byte-identical") suggests the page-only records (the 234 re-stamped no_picture_found search strings) would be lost if the page file were re-exported.
Why: the page file is a pure function of the item files: `export` copies each item's `candidates` and `no_picture_found` verbatim, and keeps an item open only while `resolved` is unrecorded AND no candidate has a data/db/platefits/ doc; the re-stamps were committed INTO the item files by 9c48d94 (a7f5dda's "byte-identical" refers to that commit's own diff, which only re-derived the page). Verified 2026-10-13 after a main merge, before my scoped portus export: 0 no_picture_found diffs across all 343 page items vs their item files.
What to do: resolve the merge by taking the NEWER `at` (the per-item regions auto-merge), verify page vs item files if in doubt, then `fr.export(fr.ROOT, site)` scoped to your own site: it writes `resolved` only into that one site's item file (write-once) and recomputes the whole page file, keeping every other branch's re-stamps.

#### The recorded `resolved` field is NOT 201's open flag: an item whose recorded doc was deleted goes back to the queue
Where: `fit/review.py` (`resolved_doc`, `export`), `data/review/*.json`, `tests/test_batch.py`
Symptom: a coverage/open check written against the item file's raw `resolved` field (`item["resolved"] is None` = open) miscounts the site as closed/uncovered once the resolving doc is later deleted - the live instances measured 2026-10-13 (task 203): aesica-q4688554 (batch auto doc rejected on sight, b22a2d2) and alligator-effigy-mound-q4732645 - both items still record `resolved: {"doc": ..., "at": ...}`, but that doc no longer exists in data/db/platefits/, so 201's derivation brings both items back into the page's open list (both present in web/data/review.json, 457 open of 457 items).
Why: `resolved` is write-once, but resolution is DERIVED: `resolved_doc` honors a recorded resolution only while the named doc file exists, then falls back to the candidates' doc existence; with none, the item is open again (b22a2d2's rule; see also the data/db/platefits section).
What to do: any open/closed counting (batch coverage checks, export-staleness expectations, page counts) goes through `review.resolved_doc(item, root) is None`, never the raw field.

#### The one-site line prints its own header BEFORE its work, and the server worker prints two-space-indented reports - a runlog filter keyed on the bare phrase "one-site line" catches the header too
Where: tools/site_done.py:326 (the header `site <sid>: the one-site line (fit -> sync -> entry -> review)`, printed before the fit/sync work), server/serve.py:251/255/257 (the fit worker's `  one-site line for <sid>: finished (exit N)` / `  one-site line for <sid>: unavailable in this tree (...)` / `  one-site line for <sid> failed: ...`), tests/test_owner_check.py (check 7, the runlog slice)
Symptom: a runlog filter or exact-match assert keyed on the phrase "one-site line" matches the site_done header as well as the worker's finished report - a count is off by one and a "the line did not run" conclusion is wrong (307d's tenth session: check 7's phrase filter caught the header, present since 300 built the line, and the exact-equality assert failed on it; the eighth session's static verification had checked the no-model/no-batch/_summary prints only and missed this one)
Why: the header announces the line's start (site_done's own stdout); the worker's indented reports confirm its end (the server process). They are different messages from different places in the log.
What to do: match the finished report by its two-space-indented shape (`  one-site line for `) - that also catches the unavailable/failed variants, which an exact-equality assert then fails on, as intended; never key a filter on the bare phrase.
